title: AI Engineer III - Enterprise Architecture
description:
The Enterprise Technology Services organization partners with every part of the American Express business to power the company's growth and innovation with trust and efficiency, and drive competitive differentiation with speed. We support the delivery and operations of technology, digital, and data capabilities, paltforms and sercices globally. Specifically, our team is responsible for the company's technology engineering, architecture, and infrastructure, providing 24X7 support to ensure an uninterrupted, high quality experience for customers and colleague. We also provide product management for core enterprise platforms, and lead technology risk and information security, enterprise data governance and platforms, digital product and design, and enterprise AI platforms on behalf of the company.

At American Express, AI is reshaping the future of commerce and refining the experiences our commercial customers and card members expect, Within AMEX Technology, we are building platforms, products and governance that enable agentic AI systems to operate responsibly and at scale across the enterprise.

Our focus is on agentic AI development: designing intelligent, adaptive systems that can plan, reason, and act across complex workflows with appropriate levels of autonomy. These systems power autonomous workflows, decision support, and customer-facing experiences—while meeting the high standards for security, explainability, reliability, and compliance required in financial services.

We partner closely with product, design, and business teams to deliver agentic capabilities that reduce operational friction, improve decision-making, and transform how customers interact, transact, and grow

The Role

As an AI Engineer – Agentic AI, you will be a hands-on builder contributing to the development of production agentic AI systems that operate on real financial data and serve real customers.

You will work alongside experienced engineers, product managers, and designers to design, build, and ship AI-powered features, while learning how to operate within a regulated, customer-facing environment. This role offers strong mentorship and opportunities to grow your technical depth in LLMs, agentic systems, and production AI engineering.

This is not a research-only role. You will write production code, contribute to system design discussions, and help operate what you build after launch, with support and guidance from more senior engineers.

What You’ll Do

  • Contribute to the design and implementation of LLM-powered and agentic product features.
  • Build and extend agentic AI workflows that reason over context, call tools, and perform actions under guidance from senior engineers.
  • Help implement and maintain retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines over financial data, with an emphasis on correctness and safety.
  • Contribute to shared AI infrastructure such as LLM services, orchestration components, and evaluation or monitoring tooling.
  • Participate in operating AI systems in production, including monitoring, debugging, and improving reliability and performance.
  • Collaborate closely with product and design partners, learning to translate customer needs into technical solutions.

Technical Environment

We don’t hire to a narrow checklist, but candidates should be excited to grow in a modern, enterprise-scale engineering environment with a focus on agentic AI.

Core engineering stack

  • Languages: Python, Go, TypeScript
  • Cloud and infrastructure: AWS and/or GCP, Kubernetes
  • APIs and services: REST, gRPC
  • Distributed systems: event-driven architectures, including Kafka

Agentic AI and ML

  • Commercial and open-source LLMs integrated into agentic workflows
  • Tooling for agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, vector storage, and evaluation
  • Schema validation and structured data handling

AI-assisted development

  • Use of AI-assisted and agentic development tools for design, implementation, testing, debugging, and refactoring
  • Learning how to apply these tools responsibly while maintaining production-quality standards
  • All systems are built to meet high standards for reliability, security, and auditability, reflecting the responsibility of deploying autonomous AI in a financial services environment.

What We’re Looking For

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering experience.
  • Some hands-on experience building or contributing to AI-powered features, LLM-based applications, or applied ML systems (professional or project-based).
  • Solid engineering fundamentals in at least one backend language (Python, Go, or TypeScript).
  • Familiarity with APIs, basic cloud concepts, and modern development practices.
  • Interest in agentic AI systems, autonomy, and AI-assisted development workflows.
  • Willingness to learn, take feedback, and grow technical ownership over time.
  • Comfort working in collaborative, cross-functional teams.
  • A strong customer mindset and curiosity about real-world problem solving.
  • Candidates are required to have a bachelor’s degree

Preferred Qualifications

  • Exposure to LLM tooling, prompt engineering, RAG, or agent frameworks through work, coursework, or personal projects.
  • Internship or early-career experience in fintech or other regulated environments.

  • Contributions to open-source projects, hackathons, or side projects related to AI or developer tooling.

    Depending on factors such as business unit requirements, the nature of the position, cost and applicable laws, American Express may provide visa sponsorship for certain positions.

title: Associate Director Finance - Remote
description:
Optum is a global organization that delivers care, aided by technology to help millions of people live healthier lives. The work you do with our team will directly improve health outcomes by connecting people with the care, pharmacy benefits, data and resources they need to feel their best. Here, you will find a culture guided by inclusion, talented peers, comprehensive benefits and career development opportunities. Come make an impact on the communities we serve as you help us advance health optimization on a global scale. Join us in making healthcare work better for everyone through people-led, responsible AI while Caring. Connecting. Growing together.


Optum Care is seeking an Associate Director of Finance to lead the Optum Care West Region Shared Services SG&A finance team. This role will provide financial leadership for shared services costs managed on behalf of the Total West Region, with responsibility for forecasting, annual planning, month-end reporting, financial analysis, chargeback management, cost allocation, department transfers, workforce planning, and executive-level financial support.


This leader will directly manage two FP&A managers and will serve as the primary finance partner for West Region leadership, sub-region finance teams, accounting, and national finance organizations. A significant focus of the role will be understanding national and enterprise chargebacks, challenging cost and allocation assumptions, identifying savings opportunities, and driving accountability for cost reductions.


The role requires solid technical FP&A capabilities, people leadership, executive communication, and the ability to operate across a complex, matrixed organization. The ideal candidate will be comfortable leading through change, improving financial transparency, establishing scalable processes, and translating complex shared services and chargeback activity into clear business insights and actions.


You'll enjoy the flexibility to work remotely * from anywhere within the U.S. as you take on some tough challenges. For all hires in the Minneapolis or Washington, D.C. area, you will be required to work in the office a minimum of four days per week.


Primary Responsibilities:

  • Lead the Optum Care West Region Shared Services SG&A finance team, including direct management, coaching, and development of two FP&A managers
  • Own forecasting, budgeting, annual planning, month-end reporting, variance analysis, and financial performance management for West Region Shared Services and assigned chargeback cost areas
  • Partner with national and enterprise finance teams to understand chargeback methodologies, guidance, cost drivers, service volumes, and forecast changes; challenge assumptions and advocate for appropriate West Region outcomes
  • Identify, quantify, and advance chargeback savings and cost reduction opportunities by analyzing trends, service utilization, unit costs, PMPM/PEPM metrics, and other relevant business drivers
  • Lead the allocation of West Region Shared Services costs to sub-regions and markets, including governance of allocation methodologies, maintenance of allocation percentages, communication of changes, and validation that costs are fully and appropriately distributed
  • Provide Total West Region chargeback reporting, high-level bridges, forecast explanations, and executive insights that clearly explain cost performance, key changes, risks, opportunities, and required actions
  • Oversee month-end activities for shared services and chargebacks, including early estimates, actual-to-forecast reviews, issue resolution, accounting coordination, and reconciliation across financial reporting systems
  • Lead financial support for department and organizational transfers within the West Region and between West, national, enterprise, and corporate organizations, ensuring accurate financial structures, forecasts, allocations, and stakeholder communication
  • Oversee workforce planning, census and headcount reviews, requisition finance approvals, GL string governance, and related financial analysis for supported shared services functions
  • Develop, refine, and maintain recurring reporting packages, forecast models, allocation tools, chargeback analyses, and management routines that improve visibility, consistency, accuracy, and accountability
  • Drive process improvement, reporting standardization, automation, and simplification opportunities to reduce manual effort and strengthen financial controls
  • Serve as a key finance partner to West Region leaders, sub-region FP&A teams, accounting, national finance teams, and cross-functional stakeholders on shared services, chargebacks, allocations, and strategic cost management
  • Lead special projects, cost deep dives, business cases, and ad hoc financial analyses tied to broader Total West Region and Optum Care SG&A priorities


You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business, or a related field
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in financial planning and analysis, accounting, finance, or related financial leadership roles
  • 3+ years of people leadership experience, including coaching, developing, and directing the work of finance professionals
  • Experience leading budgeting, forecasting, month-end reporting, variance analysis, financial modeling, and performance management processes
  • Solid understanding of SG&A, shared services, cost allocations, intercompany or intersegment chargebacks, cost center management, and financial governance
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including the ability to organize, analyze, reconcile, and summarize large datasets
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze complex cost structures, identify savings opportunities, challenge financial assumptions, and influence outcomes across a matrixed organization
  • Demonstrated solid executive communication skills with the ability to develop clear financial commentary, presentations, and recommendations for senior leaders
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, timelines, and stakeholder needs in a fast-paced, evolving environment
  • Demonstrated ability to build cross-functional relationships, influence without direct authority, and drive accountability across regional and national teams
  • Demonstrated proactive mindset with a willingness to improve processes, build scalable structures, and take ownership of complex or evolving workstreams


Preferred Qualifications:

  • MBA, CPA, CFA, or other advanced finance, accounting, or business credential
  • Experience supporting regional or enterprise shared services, corporate finance, SG&A, operating costs, chargebacks, or allocation-based financial processes
  • Experience partnering with national or enterprise functions to manage service costs, develop savings initiatives, and evaluate chargeback or allocation methodologies
  • Experience developing recurring leadership reporting packages, forecast models, allocation tools, dashboards, or standardized financial views
  • Experience driving process improvement, reporting automation, standardization, or finance transformation initiatives
  • Experience partnering with senior leaders and presenting financial results, business drivers, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions
  • Healthcare finance, managed care, provider organization, or other large matrixed organization experience
  • Knowledge of financial systems and reporting tools such as Essbase, PeopleSoft, Planful, Spotlight, Power BI, and Excel


Work Environment & Culture

  • This role will operate within Optum Care and lead financial support for West Region Shared Services SG&A and assigned chargebacks on behalf of the Total West Region
  • The team partners across West sub-regions and national finance organizations, creating an opportunity to strengthen cost management, allocation governance, standardization, scalability, and financial transparency
  • Success in this role will require leadership, collaboration, curiosity, adaptability, accountability, sound judgment, and a continuous improvement mindset


*All employees working remotely will be required to adhere to UnitedHealth Group's Telecommuter Policy


Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets, education, work experience, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, we offer benefits such as, a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). No matter where or when you begin a career with us, you'll find a far-reaching choice of benefits and incentives. The salary for this role will range from $112,700 - $193,200 annually based on full-time employment. We comply with all minimum wage laws as applicable.


Application Deadline: This will be posted for a minimum of 2 business days or until a sufficient candidate pool has been collected. Job posting may come down early due to volume of applicants.


At UnitedHealth Group, our mission is to help people live healthier lives and help make the health system work better for everyone. Together, we are shaping the future of healthcare by harnessing technology and innovation to make care simpler to navigate, more affordable and more connected for the people we serve. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcomed, valued, heard and respected, empowering people to bring their authentic selves to work and strengthening our collective impact through diverse talents, backgrounds, experiences and perspectives.

UnitedHealth Group and its affiliated brands are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer under applicable law and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by local, state, or federal laws, rules, or regulations.


UnitedHealth Group and its affiliated brands are a drug-free workplace. Candidates are required to pass a drug test before beginning employment.

title: Wellness Counselor
description:
About CT State

Connecticut State Community College (CT State) was launched on July 1, 2023, through the consolidation of Connecticut’s 12 community colleges. With campuses and satellite locations statewide, CT State serves all 169 towns and neighboring states. As the largest community college in New England, CT State is committed to providing high-quality, affordable, and accessible education that supports students’ academic, career, and personal success.

For more information about CT State Community College and the campus please visit Home - CT State

Position Details

Posted: October 13, 2026
Level: Community College Professional 19, 12-month, tenure track position
Employment Type: Standard
Hours: Full-time, 35 hours per week
Anticipated Start Date: January 2027
Work Location: CT State Gateway (20 Church Street, New Haven, CT 06510)
Work Modality: On-site; Position is not remote
Closing Date: Applications must be submitted by 5:00pm (EST) on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

Position Summary

Connecticut State Community College offers a broad range of two-year liberal arts degree programs as well as many technical, occupational and career programs. These programs attract traditional students as well as non-traditional students, including those pursuing academic training or degrees following absences from higher education, those intending to increase occupational skills and those entering higher education from other countries. Many of these students require counseling, support, and referrals on variety issues that impact their ability to successfully reach their academic and career goals.

The Wellness Counselor acts as an applied educational specialist concerned with the mental health, wellness, and overall wellbeing of students, with special attention given to the needs of those least able to act as their own advocates. This position develops and fosters extensive cooperative and collaborative relationships with faculty, staff, administrators and external stakeholders; maintains currency with emerging trends and best practices in counseling and students support; and leads the campus counseling services in the adoption of innovative practices that increase student retention and completion and eliminates equity gaps that exist between for black, LatinX, and other marginalized students when compared to white students.

The Wellness Counselor regularly collects, analyzes, and uses data to inform practice, maintain compliance with all local, state, and federal policies and laws, and ensures equitable attainment of outcomes. Wellness counselors deliver programming and direct services to students that utilize their professional expertise gained through a master’s degree in counseling, social work, or marriage and family therapy or doctoral degree in psychology.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direction of the Director of Wellness and Mental Health Services or another administrator, the Wellness Counselor is accountable for contributing to the academic, career, personal and social success of the College’s students through effective performance in these essential functional areas:

  • Wellness counseling services
    • Accountable for providing professional counseling services to community college students that contribute to their successful completion of academic, career, and personal goals.
  • Development and delivery of Wellness counseling programming
    • Accountable for participating in and contributing to the development of sound programs for guiding and counseling the College’s students in academic, personal, career, and social progress.
  • Consultation and collaboration with faculty and staff
    • Accountable for advising faculty and staff on appropriate actions and assistance for students requiring special attention.

Additional responsibilities include:

  • Attendance and participation at convocation and commencement ceremonies
  • Service on assigned committees and task forces
  • Attendance and participation at committee, staff, informational and professional meetings which may occur during evenings and weekends.

This posting outlines qualifications, experience, and skills but is not limited to the full specifications in the official job description.

Minimum Qualifications

Master’s degree in counseling, social work, or marriage and family therapy or a doctoral degree in psychology together with two (2) or more years of experience in a professional counseling capacity; or a combination of experience and training which would lead to the competencies required for the effective performance of the position’s essential duties.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Must be a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT), or PsyD or Ph.D. in Psychology with active licensure in the state of CT.
  • Experience with the full spectrum of professional counseling theory, techniques, and methods.
  • Experience with crisis counseling and intervention
  • Ability to work effectively with individuals from diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, and ethnic backgrounds, including individuals with disabilities
  • Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in a college/university counseling center.
  • Experience in mental health and wellness outreach programming.
  • Experience delivering clinical supervision to undergraduate or graduate students

Salary and Benefits

  • Salary $80,901 approximate annual

CT State offers a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Generous leave policies
  • Multiple retirement plan options
  • Comprehensive health insurance choices
  • Supplemental benefits for retirement and family protection
  • Tuition reimbursement (if applicable)

For more information, visit: Human Resources - Future Employees / Human Resources -Labor Contracts

Application Instructions

To apply, please submit the following:

  • A cover letter
  • A current resume

In your cover letter, you must clearly address how your experience and skills align with each of the required and preferred qualifications. The cover letter may be entered as text in the application system or uploaded as a single combined file with the resume.

Your resume must include the names of three (3) current professional references, including their titles, email addresses, and telephone numbers.

Important Notes:

  • Incomplete applications or those submitted after the closing date will not be considered
  • Links to external resume or profile sites will not be accepted
  • Apply online at:
  • CT State Community College cannot sponsor work visas.
  • Applicants must be authorized to work full-time in the United States

Selection Process

After the closing date, applications will be reviewed by a selection committee. Candidates selected for further consideration will be those who best meet the minimum and preferred qualifications and who submitted all required materials by the deadline.

The selection process may include interviews and practical exercises (e.g., written, technical, or simulation exercises). Finalists will be recommended to the Hiring Manager for final selection.

Background Screening

Employment offers are contingent upon:

  • Proof of eligibility to work under the Immigration Reform and Control Act (IRCA)
  • Successful completion of a background check, including granting permission to contact current and previous employers for verification, reference checks, criminal history, and, when applicable, credit or driving history checks

CT State is committed to maintaining a safe campus community.

Equity Statement

Connecticut State Community College commits to bold and disruptive change by actively identifying, naming, and dismantling structural racism, systemic poverty, and other barriers; establishing equitable and anti-racist policies and practices; and empowering students, faculty, staff, and administrators to advance racial, social, and economic justice. Our core collective responsibility is to continuously assess practices and policies and transform the world we live in by eliminating inequities.

Continuing Notice of Nondiscrimination

CT State Community College does not discriminate on the basis of age, ancestry, color, national origin, gender identity or expression, genetic information, learning disability, marital status, intellectual disability, physical disability (including but not limited to blindness), present or past history of mental disability, prior criminal record, race, religious creed, sex (including pregnancy and sexual harassment), sexual orientation, retaliation for previously opposed discrimination or coercion, veteran status, victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, and/or trafficking or any other federal or state protected class in its employment, programs, and activities, unless the provisions of Section 46a-80(b) or 46a-81(b) of the Connecticut General Statutes are controlling or there are bona fide occupational qualifications excluding persons in one of the above protected groups.

For information regarding the nondiscrimination, disability, and Title IX policies/procedures, contact: Nicholas D'Agostino, Director of Equity and Civil Rights, CT State Community College, 185 Main Street, New Britain, CT 06051, 860-612-7075 or nicholas.dagostino@ctstate.edu.

title: Validation - Engineer I / II - Project Farma

title: Business Modeling - Applied AI Modeling Executive Director

title: Lead Solutions Analyst - Data Catalog
description:
Are you ready to lead at the intersection of data strategy, governance, and enterprise technology delivery? At JPMorganChase, we believe that the right data — governed well, delivered reliably, and made accessible — is a competitive advantage. This is your opportunity to shape that future.

As a Lead Solutions Analyst at JPMorganChase within the Corporate Data and Analytics Services team, you will play a pivotal role in advancing the firm's data strategy by designing and delivering enterprise-scale data solutions across the Corporate Technology organization. You will drive the execution of key data initiatives — including the Corporate Data Catalog, Data Lineage, Entitlements, and Data Quality frameworks — while collaborating with engineering teams, senior stakeholders, and Chief Data Officers to ensure high-quality, accessible, and reliable data assets. Your work will directly support the firm's vision of a self-service, fully observable data platform that embraces data mesh and data product principles, enabling domain-driven ownership and consistent data management at scale.

Job responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end delivery of regulatory technology programs with regulator-reportable commitments, embedding control and evidence requirements into milestone exit criteria to ensure programs remain continuously audit-ready
  • Own and operate a single intake and prioritization model across multiple competing senior stakeholder organizations, converting ad-hoc demand into a published, predictable roadmap with accountable delivery cadence
  • Drive on-time milestone delivery against committed dates by managing agile delivery rhythms with engineering teams and proactively resolving cross-team dependencies and delivery risks
  • Influence and secure engineering capacity and resources from teams outside direct reporting lines, negotiating scope trade-offs directly with Chief Data Officers and senior leadership
  • Apply deep expertise in metadata management, data lineage, data governance lifecycle, data contracts, data tiering, and industry catalog standards to shape platform direction and ensure alignment with firmwide standards
  • Instrument and analyze platform usage signals to diagnose adoption blockers, re-sequence roadmaps in response, and drive measurable enterprise-scale adoption through roadshows, enablement sessions, and self-serve onboarding materials
  • Own the executive narrative for a multi-stakeholder platform, running senior governance forums and reporting milestone and risk status to senior leadership and regulatory and audit stakeholders
  • Partner with engineering leads on sprint planning and backlog refinement to ensure roadmap commitments are reflected in sprint scope and delivery risks are resolved proactively
  • Advance the firm's data mesh and data product strategy by fostering domain-driven data ownership, enabling self-service data platforms, and treating data as a product to ensure quality and reliability

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Formal training or certification on solutions analysis concepts and 5+ years applied experience
  • Proven track record delivering technology programs with regulatory reporting obligations, including embedding audit-ready controls and evidence requirements into program delivery frameworks
  • Demonstrated experience running a structured demand intake and prioritization model across multiple senior stakeholder organizations, with accountability for end-to-end agile delivery
  • Experience influencing at the Managing Director level and above, securing resources from teams outside direct reporting lines and negotiating scope trade-offs with senior data leadership
  • Deep working knowledge of metadata management, data lineage, data governance lifecycle, data contracts, and industry catalog standards such as DCAT and DPROD
  • Proven ability to drive measurable platform adoption at enterprise scale, including diagnosing adoption blockers and leading enablement programs for technical and executive audiences
  • Strong executive communication skills with experience owning governance reporting, running senior forums, and framing complex trade-offs for leadership decision-making

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Experience with AI-ready data product enablement and familiarity with data mesh principles and domain-driven data ownership models
  • Familiarity with regulatory frameworks such as BCBS 239 or equivalent regulator-reportable data governance standards
  • Experience collaborating with engineering teams on sprint planning and backlog refinement to align roadmap commitments with delivery execution
  • Knowledge of data catalog, data quality, data entitlements, and data retention and destruction frameworks in a large-scale enterprise environment
  • Background working within a federated technology organization, coordinating across multiple lines of business or technology domains to deliver shared platform capabilities

title: Leader of AI & Data Platforms
description:
Leader of AI and Data Leader

Function/Department: Information Technology / Data & AI
Reports to: Chief Information Officer (CIO) & Vice President, IT
Location: Chandler, AZ or Hollister, CA — fully on-site
FLSA: Exempt


Job Summary
PacSci EMC is seeking a hands-on AI engineering leader to accelerate enterprise AI adoption and build the governed data foundations that enable practical, secure business solutions. This leader personally develops, deploys, and sustains production AI and data capabilities while leading a small team across data engineering, architecture, and application and analytics development.
The AI and Data Leader leads technical architecture and data readiness for the Palantir Foundry initiative in partnership with the business SME leader and PMO, while advancing enterprise data stewardship, lifecycle management, and self-service tools. The role combines technical execution, team development, and executive influence in an evolving environment. It also participates in the Ralliant Technology & Growth Council, with up to 20% allocation, contributing to enterprise architecture reviews, innovation, standards, and cross-operating-company technology direction.


Responsibilities
• Evaluate and recommend secure, compliant AI tools; personally implement and operationalize priority solutions that improve productivity and enable business teams to use AI effectively.
• Identify and prioritize AI opportunities across Planning, Buying, Manufacturing Operations, Factory Management, Engineering, PMO, and other business functions; translate operating challenges into practical solutions and measurable outcomes.
• Lead and develop a small team across data engineering, architecture, and Power BI/Power Platform development; provide technical coaching, establish delivery priorities, and build team capability as business needs evolve.
• Lead technical architecture, data readiness, and implementation support for Palantir Foundry in partnership with the business SME leader, who retains overall program delivery accountability, and PMO; coordinate appropriate technology resources and architectural decisions.
• Establish enterprise data warehousing, stewardship, and lifecycle-management practices, including labeling, lineage, retention, role-based access, auditability, and clearly defined data ownership.
• Use Microsoft Purview to support data governance and lifecycle-management practices across priority data domains.
• Build and maintain production-grade pipelines, transformations, data models, and reusable integration patterns; develop governed ontologies, lightweight applications, and self-service data products as business priorities require.
• Partner with manufacturing engineering and other technical specialists on SCADA/OT data integration, reference data products, and anomaly-detection use cases; establish data architecture standards and document interfaces and operational runbooks.
• Enable business users through training, practical playbooks, quick-start templates, and hands-on collaboration; support citizen development within appropriate access and compliance guardrails.
• Partner with analytics developers to deliver dashboards, signals, and triggers that improve operational visibility and actionability, including order execution and cost tracking.
• Own reliability of AI and data assets through monitoring, observability, performance tuning, troubleshooting, and ongoing production support; implement reusable quality checks and alerts.
• Present technology options and recommendations to leaders with clear cost, impact, risk, and implementation tradeoffs; collaborate on decisions and balance immediate delivery needs with enterprise standards.
• Define baselines and track solution adoption and business impact, including hours saved, manual effort reduced, automated transactions, efficiency, revenue enablement, and supply-chain execution performance.
• Maintain an actionable opportunity backlog, data product catalog, access reviews, and governance routines aligned with PMO practices; contribute to Ralliant technology and architecture forums.


First 6 to 12 Months Focus and Deliverables
• Build relationships with manufacturing, quality, program management, supply chain, and other business partners to understand pain points and establish a prioritized AI opportunity pipeline.
• Support the Palantir initiative through sound technical architecture, data readiness, and delivery of initial governed data products and Foundry assets.
• Implement an enterprise data layer strategy with clear ownership, warehousing standards, lifecycle practices, and appropriate governance and access safeguards.
• Expand secure self-service AI tools and adoption through training, practical use cases, and reusable development standards.
• Demonstrate sustained production delivery and measurable business improvements in productivity, manual effort, efficiency, revenue enablement, or supply-chain execution.


Qualifications
• 5+ years in analytics, data platforms, AI enablement, or data governance roles, with proven hands-on delivery.
• Demonstrated personal experience building, deploying, and sustaining production AI and data solutions, including production-grade pipelines and appropriate operational safeguards.
• Strong hands-on proficiency with SQL and Python/PySpark; experience with data modeling, orchestration, and observability.
• Experience with Microsoft Purview and enterprise data governance, stewardship, or lifecycle management.
• Demonstrated ability to learn enterprise data platforms, guide architectural decisions, and coordinate technical delivery across business and technology teams.
• Working knowledge of Power BI or similar analytics tools and the ability to partner with developers on governed self-service analytics.
• Strong cross-functional influence and executive communication; ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences and support recommendations with evidence and business impact.
• Ability to lead technical work, coach colleagues, and collaborate effectively while remaining personally involved in engineering and delivery.
• Comfort operating in an evolving environment, prioritizing amid ambiguity, developing practical prototypes, and carrying solutions through implementation and ongoing support.


Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with Palantir Foundry, including pipelines, ontology, and application development; strongly preferred.
• Background in aerospace and defense or other highly regulated industries with strict data and compliance requirements, such as ITAR, FAR/DFARS, or DCAA.
• Familiarity with controlled unclassified information (CUI), FedRAMP requirements, and secure cloud deployment practices.
• Working knowledge of SCADA/OT data environments, ERP/MES/PLM data structures, and manufacturing execution workflows.
• Experience building AI or data capabilities in a startup, technology disruptor, or similarly resource-constrained environment, with demonstrated implementation results.
• Familiarity with Lean principles and structured problem solving; ability to balance rapid delivery with compliance and sustainable operations.


Employment Eligibility
Due to U.S. Government contract requirements applicable to this position, only U.S. citizens are eligible for employment in this role.

title: Lead Data Scientist, Credit Risk
location: Chicago, IL, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA
description:
About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Credit Risk Data Scientist who is data-driven, has strong analytical and technical skills, and operates with a high degree of ownership. In this role, you will lead the credit strategy that lets Chime lend to people before they have a relationship with us — starting with Instant Loans for new members (top of funnel) and expanding to future unsecured credit products such as credit cards. You'll develop risk policies and strategies to manage credit risk throughout the member lifecycle, and you'll work as a trusted cross-functional partner with product, growth, data engineering, machine learning, and analytics teams, interacting with business stakeholders across many departments.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Own credit strategy for new-to-Chime applicants across the member lifecycle, starting with Instant Loans for prospects (top of funnel) and extending to future unsecured products such as credit cards and/or lines of credit
  • Develop and evolve channel-specific credit policies (pre-approval / prescreen, direct mail, open application, referrals, and affiliates) that support growth while balancing risk, unit economics, and member experience
  • Design and continuously iterate acquisition, loan amount / line assignment, pricing, line management, repayment, and collections strategies
  • Leverage credit bureau (e.g., Experian), alternative, and internal Chime data to underwrite applicants with no prior Chime relationship; build credit models and policies hands-on and in partnership with our DSML team
  • Lead test-and-learn: design and read out champion/challenger tests and controlled ramps, and quantify trade-offs among approvals, losses, direct deposit conversion, and lifetime value
  • Partner with Finance and Strategy to size new channels and forecast approval funnels, vintage losses, and unit economics; set launch criteria, guardrails, and expansion triggers
  • Collaborate with data teams to build data infrastructure and early-read monitoring and dashboards (first payment default, delinquency, vintage and roll rates) that help senior management understand credit risk trends and exposures
  • Work with cross-functional teams including DSML, Product, Design, Engineering, and Decision Platform to test and implement risk models and strategies in production, including accurate adverse action reasons
  • Partner with Compliance, Legal, Fair Lending, Model Risk Management, Fraud, and our bank partners to document, approve, and govern credit policies
  • Mentor and work collaboratively with other credit risk data scientists to develop strategies, share knowledge, and raise the team's analytical bar

To thrive in this role, you have

  • A Master's degree (required) in Statistics, Economics, Engineering, Math, Finance, Computer Science, or another quantitative discipline; a PhD is a plus
  • 7+ years of analytical or data science experience in Financial Services, preferably at a FinTech company
  • 4+ years of experience building and managing risk for unsecured credit products such as installment loans, lines of credit, or credit cards; acquisition / underwriting experience strongly preferred
  • Hands-on experience with credit bureau data and prescreen, pre-approval, or direct mail credit programs
  • Experience with credit furnishing, bankruptcies, delinquency, and write-off policies, and working knowledge of consumer lending regulation (FCRA, ECOA / Reg B, fair lending, adverse action)
  • Excellent SQL and Python skills, advanced Microsoft Excel skills, and experience working in Looker or a similar business intelligence tool
  • A strong grounding in statistics and machine learning for credit, including scorecards / gradient-boosted models, swap-set analysis, vintage analysis, and experiment design
  • Hands-on, detail-oriented leader with exceptional communication skills who can explain a trade-off to executives and defend the math behind it
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, complex environment and meet ambitious deadlines while ensuring flawless completion
  • A strong passion for Chime's mission and solving challenging analytical problems for the business
  • Nice to have: subprime or near-prime lending, affiliate or marketplace lending, credit card line management, or cash-flow / alternative-data underwriting experience

title: Enrollment and Onboarding Supervisor I
description:
Job Function Summary

Involves designing, conducting, promoting, evaluating and supporting health professions education programs in compliance with organizational objectives and nationally accepted accreditation standards and requirements. Supports learners (including but not limited to faculty, residents, clinical fellows, graduate or undergraduate learners, practicing or licensed professionals) in areas such as curriculum, teaching and learning activities, scheduling, core competencies, assessment and evaluations. Coordinates all activities associated with ongoing administration of health professions education programs.

Generic Scope

Provides immediate supervision to a unit or group of operational or technical employees. A portion of time may be spent performing individual tasks related to the unit; however, supervisory activities must constitute a primary part of the job. Supervises unit operations to ensure compliance with departmental or organizational policies, procedures, and defined internal controls. Ensures accountability and stewardship of department resources (operational, financial, and human) in compliance with departmental standards and procedures.

Custom Scope

The onboarding, enrollment and visiting student programs supervisor will directly oversee the day-to-day operations for the functions that include onboarding of all learners, enrollment processes and the visiting student programs within the Undergraduate Medical Education department. This position will directly supervise the work of 1 onsite visiting student coordinator and 1 front office operations coordinator and will be responsible for the quality and quantity of work. The supervisor will monitor progress of duties and work-flow to ensure consistency across the department.

The supervisor will have two direct reports and will work to ensure the front office environment is welcoming, available and service oriented to all learners as well as ensuring the visiting student program that serves close to 300 students for elective rotations and the enrollment and onboarding services that are required for each learner is delivered timely, accurately and efficiently. The supervisor will be responsible for creating and updating processes as well as tracking student enrollment and providing in-depth reports on volume and infrastructure needs.

Department Overview

UCSF Fresno is a regional campus of UCSF School of Medicine located in California’s central valley. The Department of Undergraduate Medical Education (UME) is the administrative unit that oversees all core health professions education programs (Medical and Allied Health) for the regional campus including oversight of the San Joaquin Valley Program in Medical Education (PRIME). UME provides services for 100 or more third-year students from UCSF campus as well as close to 300 visiting students from accredited medical education programs across the United States.

UME works collaboratively and in communities of practice with our medical education partners in Student Experience and the Assessment, Curriculum & Evaluation teams at UCSF School of Medicine. UCSF Fresno also has over 300 trainees in several accredited Graduate Medical Education Residency & Fellowship programs. The UCSF Fresno UME Office is responsible for implementation of all strategic directives for medical student education at the Fresno campus and for ensuring that those who serve undergraduate student learners are actively engaged in the highest quality learning and teaching environment with a strong commitment to UCSF’s PRIDE values.

The UME Department currently has a staff of 10 including an Assistant Dean, Program Director, 1 manager, 1 supervisor and 6 administrative staff to provide services in student experience, engagement, wellness and advising and support as well as curriculum, assessments and evaluation for all core undergraduate learners. In addition to our core learners, UME oversees a robust visiting student program that provides elective rotations to learners giving them an opportunity to interact with our GME residency programs.

Onboarding, Enrollment & Visiting Student Oversight

Under general direction of the Director of UME carries out all key responsibilities and works to meet the educational needs of program participants through coordinated onboarding, enrollment and visiting student programs and processes.

  • Supervise the group of visiting student program coordinator and front office operations coordinator and also perform some functions of the work related to enrollment which includes application uploading and processing, and working with affiliate partners to obtain hospital credentials necessary for the learner’s experience.
  • Work with key registration partners to ensure student credentials are obtained as needed for affiliate clinical site placements.
  • Prepare and present the annual enrollment data report to leadership which includes numbers of students, numbers of electives as well as residency rotation to interview tracking.
  • Ensure that all onboarding for every learner including visiting students, allied health and advanced practice professionals, dental students, PRIME students and traditional UCSF students who are part of our core learning group is completed on time.
  • Become part of the Operations Leadership Team to discuss and plan for program growth, changes or new systems implementation.
  • Perform human resources and supervisory functions including responsibility for two staff who will be coordinating all activities associated with regular and ongoing student enrollment, onboarding and application processing.

Database and Application Systems Management

  • Monitors all databases and application portals of student files, ensures application portal is live and functional for learners to access, monitors program documentation, enrollment, application process and onboarding to ensure compliance with established standards.
  • Tracks individual student compliance.
  • Develops and maintains program processes for documentation to meet regulatory requirements.
  • Oversee student application process and affiliate onboarding for all learners rotating on clinical electives and rotations in Fresno to include Traditional UCSF students, PRIME students, visiting 3rd or 4th year students, international students, contracted students, all non-core allied health professionals.

Administrative Lead for Undergraduate Medical Education Committee

  • Leads Undergraduate Medical Education Committee (UMEC) preparations with oversight of the Operations Coordinator.
  • Ensures reports and documents are completed and compiled for leadership to present at the quarterly UMEC.
  • Oversee the work of the coordinator who will perform administrative support duties for the Undergraduate Medical Education Committee.
  • Ensure development of agenda in conjunction with Assistant Dean and department director.
  • Supervisor will update membership roster as needed annually to include new resident appointees as well as student representatives.
  • Ensure that all members have access to committee charge and roster details.
  • Ensure systems are in place to maintain historical archives using online platforms.

Financial and Fund Management

  • Manage Clerkship fund and associated accounts used for enrollment and visiting student programs.
  • Apply annual updates and increases as directed by leadership.
  • Monitors the budget, approves clerkship related charges and communicate significant changes to upper management.
  • Prepare internal reports.

General Administration and Human Resources

  • General administrative & Human Resource duties and other duties as assigned.
  • Attend UME general and operational staff meetings.
  • Perform HR functions for team including annual reviews, professional development and quality improvement.
  • Oversee the orientation process for new incoming learners.
  • Provide support during the absence of other administrative staff.
  • Assist with UME activities and events related to program growth and expansion.

Required Qualifications

  • Ability to work full time onsite in Fresno, Ca.
  • Thorough knowledge of relevant policies and regulatory requirements. Solid knowledge of medical education program requirements. Thorough knowledge of medical education industry.
  • Thorough knowledge of administrative analysis and operations research. Demonstrated ability to develop and implement processes and systems. Thorough knowledge of the administrative and operational implications in a program. Ability to solve problems and suggest solutions through critical thinking process.
  • Effective communication skills with peers, learners, faculty, and other education program coordinators / managers.
  • Proficient skills in training and guiding employees on site-specific administrative and operational processes. Demonstrated ability to motivate and inspire staff to improve center services.
  • Excellent organizational skills, analytical, and demonstrated attention to detail. Ability to complete work and meet established deadlines and prioritize effectively in an accurate and timely manner, and to manage short and competing deadlines. Ability to organize assigned staff and sub-unit operations in an efficient and effective manner.
  • Knowledge of data management, documentation methods used in investigating and presenting findings about the program. Skills include statistical analysis of data across databases and systems.
  • Working knowledge of department, organization, HR and university policies and processes. Working knowledge of relevant industry federal, state and local laws and regulations including national accrediting organizations and state and federal licensing and regulatory offices.
  • Demonstrated record of excellent attendance and reliability to help manage the office and serve as a lead.
  • Ability to solve problems and suggest solutions through critical thinking process.
  • Working knowledge of educational software and technologies to promote a wide-range of teaching and learning goals.

Required Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training and three years of experience at least one in a lead/supervisory role.

Preferred Education

  • Master's degree in related area preferred.

Licenses

None listed.

This role is perfect for someone who thrives on delivering exceptional service in a fun, dynamic environment. The Key Holder Associates are responsible for meeting company guest service standards in their interactions with all store guests; accurately and efficiently processing guest sales transactions; restocking merchandise; and completing other tasks as assigned by store management.
Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities

Promptly greets store guests and offers assistance to provide quality guest service to everyone who shops in the store.
Consistently practice suggestively selling to create and increase sales by using open-ended questions to engage the guest in conversation, suggesting promotional items and attempting to add on to every sale.

Follow Event Network and hotel appearance and dress standards.
Process all transactions in the cash register system in an accurate and efficient manner. This includes but is not limited to cash and credit card payments, employee discounts, guest room charges, hotel property charges.
Complete store paperwork and other procedures required for the operation of the store. This includes, but is not limited, printing register reports, performing cycle counts, and opening and closing store procedures.
Recognize security risks and protect company and store assets. Know how to prevent and properly handle situations, which could result in loss to the store and company.
Follow all applicable state and federal laws and company policies and procedures for store operations, time keeping procedures, hotel, loss prevention and human resources policies and procedures.
Work together as a team with all staff to achieve store goals and contribute toward creating a positive work environment.

Skills / Qualifications

Experience as a keyholder or supervisor in a retail environment.
Merchandising experience organizing and presenting products that are visually appealing.
Friendly, outgoing personality with a service mindset.
Must be 21 for Liquor sales
Position requires flexible availability, including weekends, holidays, morning and evening shifts.

Physical Demands – The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the Key Holder Associate is frequently required to stand up to 8 hours (except during breaks and meal periods required by law and company policy); walk and use hands to finger, handle, or feel. The employee is occasionally required to reach with hands and arms; climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.

title: Workplace AI Enablement Lead
location: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Egypt, Latvia, Lithuania, North Macedonia, Serbia, Slovenia, Spain, Tunisia
description:
General Information

Location
Work at Home
Job ID
13212
Job Category
Information Technology (IT)
Language Requirement
English

Description & requirements

Description

At Transcom, we are a global customer experience specialist with over 35 000 employees across the globe. We have already successfully deployed cutting-edge CX products, including AI Agents, Voice automations and real-time translation solutions that transform how millions of people experience customer service every day.


Now we are turning that same firepower inwards. We are looking for someone to make 35 000 colleagues measurably better at their jobs by giving each of them access to the right AI support toolset.


Join Transcom as a Workplace AI Enablement Lead


You are not starting from a blank page. Google's AI suite is Transcom's standard and is already deployed across the business, our security, privacy and compliance colleagues have already done the hard work of clearing the way. Pockets of the organisation are already running on this: early adopters who built their own notebooks, teams who rewired how they handle documentation, people who will happily show you a workflow they invented themselves.


What we need now is someone to take that momentum and make it the norm. The proof of concept phase is behind us. This is now about scale and a broader adoption across the company.


You will be the person who sits down with the HR team, a workforce planner or a country manager and shows them the one workflow that gives them back three hours a week, and then builds the network that spreads it without you in the room.


Your audience is deliberately not IT and not developers. It is everyone else. Your success is measured in habits changed, not features demoed.

This role is open to candidates inCroatia ideallybut we will consider candidates based in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Egypt, Latvia, Lithuania, Macedonia, Serbia, Slovenia, Spain or Tunisia.


You will


  • Own adoption:Take e.g. Gemini Enterprise and Google NotebookLM from "used well by some" to "indispensable to most", and be accountable for a measurable, visible spike in real daily and weekly usage across the business

  • Build the champion network:Our early adopters already exist and are already sharing — informally, generously and without much structure. You will find them, formalise the network, train them and give them the backing of a proper mandate, so they can sell the tools inside their own teams far better than any central function ever could. Adoption cannot be forced top-down — you will make it grow sideways

  • Create virtual teammates:Some teams have already built their own AI assistants and are seeing the benefit. You will make that repeatable — teaching leaders and contributors to configure specialised notebooks, reusable templates and custom instructions for the routine documentation, analysis and onboarding work that eats their week

  • Cut through the noise:Workspace AI ships new features constantly. You will vet them ruthlessly, ignore what is merely clever, and translate what is genuinely useful into plain, non-technical business language

  • Hold the line on safety:You are not inventing our guardrails from scratch — our security, privacy and ethical AI principles are established, and the specialists behind them are engaged and ready to support you. Your job is to make those boundaries land in everyday practice, so people know exactly what they can put into a prompt, and why they still have to check the answer

  • Prove it: Gather the field intelligence from your champions, build on the success stories we already have, and give leadership short, honest updates with the adoption metrics behind them


What's in it for YOU

  • A genuinely rare mandate: a global company that has already made the AI investment and is now serious about the most important part – getting people to actually drive value out of it

  • Visibility. This role touches every function and every geography.

  • The freedom to shape your own approach and actively influence how ways of working evolve across the organization

  • International and inclusive environment, that makes you feel supported, encouraged and welcome from day one

  • A personalized development plan and a dedicated education budget

  • Flexible work schedule and life-work balance


To be successful in this role, the following is needed:

  • A practitioner, not a commentator:real hands-on experience with Gemini Enterprise, Gemini Advanced and NotebookLM, or close equivalents such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise or Claude – you use these tools daily, not occasionally

  • Deep working knowledge of a collaboration suite (Google Workspace strongly preferred: Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet)

  • A translator:a proven ability to explain complex AI capability in simple, non-technical language to people who did not ask for a tech lesson

  • A pragmatist: instinctive bias towards workflows that save time over features that impress engineers

  • An influencer without authority: high credibility among peers, and a track record of inspiring, coaching and building networks of advocates without a reporting line to lean on

  • Confidence facilitating live sessions – demos, lunch-and-learns, open Q&A – and the ability to hold a room, including a sceptical one

  • A solid understanding of and genuine respect for enterprise compliance, security and data privacy principles

  • Experience in digital adoption, enablement, product or platform ownership, or a technical/analytical role in a large distributed organisation

  • A degree in Business Administration, Technology Management, Communication or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

  • English verbal and written is required (C1 or higher level)

  • Well-developed communication skills, a team player mentality and a willingness to share ideas and best practice



If you are tired of watching great AI tools go unused, and you would rather change how a global company works than write another strategy deck about it, let's talk.

Apply now with a full CV in English.

Closing date for applications is Wednesday 30th September 2026.

What Life at Transcom is like

At Transcom, we're relentlessly committed. To our clients and each other. Every day, someone starts their journey with Transcom. Taking the potential they have today and turning it into skills for the future. Getting recognized for working hard, being a team player, and supporting others. Championing positive, lasting change in their teams and communities. That's just how we are at Transcom. Here we care and root for each other. You're included, just as you are, from day one. And with the right mindset, there's no end to how far we can go together.

Dodd Frank/Truth in Lending Act

This position is subject to the Dodd Frank/Truth in Lending Act qualification requirements for Loan Originators. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMC's review of your criminal conviction history, credit report, information available through NMLS, and any other information relevant to a determination by JPMC that you demonstrate financial responsibility, good character, and general fitness for the position. Note that any felony conviction within the last seven years will disqualify you from consideration for this position. Your continued employment in this position would be contingent upon compliance with Truth in Lending Act/Dodd Frank Loan Originator requirements.

In addition, this position requires National Mortgage Licensing System and Registry (NMLS) registration under the SAFE Act of 2008. As such, upon active employment with JPMorgan Chase, you will be required to either register on NMLS, or to update your existing registration as necessary to grant access to and reflect your employment with JPMorgan Chase. Your continued employment in this position with JPMorgan Chase is contingent upon compliance with the SAFE Act, including successful registration immediately after your start date, and timely completion of annual renewal and required updates thereafter.

Team members have backgrounds in project finance, emerging markets, structured finance, and commodities, and regularly collaborate with colleagues in M&A advisory, debt capital markets, derivatives structuring, and other coverage and product groups.   • Bachelor’s Degree required, preferably in accounting, finance, economics, or a related field

  • Strong quantitative and financial analysis skills

  • Experience developing project finance models in Excel

  • Previous experience creating marketing materials and presentations in PowerPoint

title: Residential Aide
description:
Program: Days Inn | 437 39th Street Brooklyn, NY 11232
What You’ll Do
If you want to help struggling and vulnerable families, this could be a great opportunity for you. Days Inn, located in Brooklyn, New York is an emergency shelter for asylum-seeking families with children. As a Residential Aide, you’ll be responsible for helping to ensure the safety of our clients, the security of our facility and grounds, and the orderly operation of the facility during your shift. You’ll also work directly with our clients to ensure that they attend required internal and external meetings, escorting them when necessary, and collaborate with Social Services team members to ensure client issues are addressed and there is continuity and consistent communication throughout a client's stay.
Your responsibilities will include:

Conducting Intake/Orientation for new clients, which includes explaining processes, rules, and regulations; copying and filing IDs; and assigning rooms.

Conducting and documenting patrols to ensure client compliance with site rules and regulations to ensure health and safety.

Ensuring that clients receive any notices of meetings and appointments from the Social Services team on a timely basis, escorting clients to meetings and appointments when necessary.

Distributing meals received from our food service vendors to clients.

Managing processes for inventorying and securing possessions of clients who don’t return to the site for various reasons.

Using the DHS CARES system to track vacancies, code clients in and out, print rosters, etc.

Documenting any incidents that occur during your shift.

You’re a great fit for this role if you have:

High School Diploma or equivalent OR equivalent experience and skills.

Bilingual fluency is strongly preferred.

FDNY F-02 Fireguard Certificate required (30-day allowance to obtain).

NYC Food Handler’s Certification (If you don’t have this, we’ll give you 30 days to take the free online course and we’ll pay the exam fee).

Work experience in a residential facility.

Experience and capacity to work with people experiencing homelessness or other disadvantaged people.

Strong relationship and customer service skills.

Familiarity with Service Fusion and Syteline (or equivalent service dispatch and ERP systems).

This position serves as a catch-all production role, assisting with tasks such as food preparation, cooking, baking, packaging, sanitation, and general production support. The role can be taught to individuals with no prior experience and is ideal for candidates interested in learning food production in a fast-paced environment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Essential duties include, but are not limited to, the following:
Food Preparation & Production

Prepare, cook, and bake hot and cold food items according to recipes, production schedules, and safety standards
Assist with baking operations, including mixing, weighing, portioning, and monitoring product quality
Wash, peel, cut, chop, slice, grind, and prepare vegetables, fruits, meats, poultry, and seafood
Measure and weigh ingredients accurately using scales and measuring tools
Assemble ingredients to produce finished or semi-finished products
Carry pans, kettles, luggers, trays, and other food containers to and from workstations, ovens, stoves, coolers, and refrigerators

Packaging & Distribution

Package, wrap, label, price, and prepare finished goods for storage or distribution
Store food products in designated areas following FIFO (First In, First Out) practices
Separate, organize, and arrange pallets or products for distribution to stores or departments

Sanitation & Safety

Maintain a clean, safe, and sanitary work area at all times
Clean and sanitize workstations, equipment, utensils, and production areas
Wash dishes, pots, pans, trays, and production tools as needed
Remove trash and recyclables and maintain waste areas
Follow all food safety, sanitation, and workplace safety standards
Report safety hazards, equipment issues, or quality concerns to supervisors promptly

General Responsibilities

Follow all Bristol Farms and Lazy Acres policies, procedures, and standards as outlined in the employee handbook
Meet and exceed company standards for food quality, safety, cleanliness, and efficiency
Perform additional production-related duties as assigned

Education and/or Experience

No prior experience required; training will be provided
Prior food production, kitchen, bakery, or manufacturing experience is helpful but not required

Language Skills

Ability to understand, speak, read, and follow instructions in English or Spanish
Ability to read basic recipes, labels, and safety instructions

Mathematical Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide using whole numbers
Ability to measure ingredients accurately using standard units of measure

Reasoning Ability

Ability to follow written, verbal, and demonstrated instructions
Ability to apply common sense to carry out routine production tasks

Physical Demands
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to:

Stand and walk for extended periods of time
Use hands and fingers to handle, feel, and operate tools, equipment, and controls
Reach with hands and arms; bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl as needed
Lift and/or move up to 50 pounds frequently and occasionally lift heavier items
Perform repetitive motions and physically demanding tasks
Have close vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus

Work Environment

Production environments may include kitchens, bakeries, commissaries, and refrigerated areas
Employees may regularly work in cold environments (approximately 41°F or below)
Noise levels may be moderate to loud
Exposure to heat, cold, moving mechanical parts, and kitchen equipment is common

title: Caster Operator
description:
Caster Operator - $24.90-$25.82/hr. + shift premium
Charge and operate electric induction melting and holding furnaces by performing the following duties.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Starts casting process.
Cleans and launders as necessary.
Prepares and sets up caster to start the casting process, e.g., changes molds, positions starter bars, and performs miscellaneous production maintenance tasks.
Operates the shaker and feeder to charge melting furnaces.
Loads pre-weighed scrap metal into the furnace using a shaker.
Operates furnace control panel to regulate furnace heat to specified temperatures by watching the color of metal thermocouple.
Observes the color and temperature of the metal and adjusts controls to maintain the specified temperature. Adjustments to spray rings are made as necessary.
Skims impurities from the surface of metal using a rake and/or a mechanical deslagger.
Operates a pressurized holding furnace.
Operates the chip-melting furnace.
Operates the melting furnace.
Pours over the melting furnaces into the holding furnace.
Removes test sample of molten metal from melting furnaces and sends to the lab.
Stamp the furnace number of sample and identification onto the sample.
Mixes molten metal with an air lance when required. Adds additional metal to the furnace to comply with specifications.
Will be trained to drive hi-lo.
Maintains work area to acceptable housekeeping standards.
Meets quality and productivity standards at all times.
Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee regularly works near moving mechanical parts and is regularly exposed to fumes or airborne particles. In these areas, employees are required to wear battery-operated filtering helmets. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.
8.5-hour shifts: Afternoon shift 2:30 pm-11:00pm; Midnight shift 10:30 pm-7:00am

title: Senior Program Management Analyst (AUKUS)

Position: Senior Program Management Analyst

Overview
ITC Defense is seeking a Senior Program Management Analyst to support strategic initiatives focused on the Submarine Industrial Base (SIB) and AUKUS programs. This position provides programmatic support to high-visibility defense initiatives that strengthen international partnerships and advance critical submarine industrial capabilities. Working in a dynamic, collaborative environment, the Senior Program Analyst will help ensure effective program execution, cross-functional coordination, and alignment with customer objectives while supporting the continued growth and success of complex defense programs.

What You'll Do

  • Support end-to-end execution of international defense programs while ensuring compliance with applicable contract requirements, ITAR, EAR, Foreign Military Sales (FMS), and other U.S. export control regulations.
  • Serve as the primary liaison among U.S. Government customers, foreign military partners, commercial suppliers, and cross-functional internal teams to support successful program execution.
  • Develop and manage integrated master schedules, budgets, risk mitigation plans, and contract deliverables to ensure program objectives are achieved within cost, schedule, and quality requirements.
  • Support Submarine Industrial Base (SIB) and AUKUS initiatives by collaborating with industry partners, suppliers, and stakeholders to enhance industrial capacity, workforce capability, and mission readiness.
  • Prepare and deliver executive-level briefings, program status reports, and other customer-facing deliverables.
  • Support workforce planning and staffing activities necessary to meet program requirements.
  • Monitor program performance, identify risks, and recommend corrective actions to ensure successful execution.
  • Maintain effective coordination with engineering, legal, compliance, supply chain, and other internal stakeholders throughout the program lifecycle.
  • Travel periodically to Washington, D.C., and other customer or partner locations as required.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Program Management, or a related field.
  • Minimum ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience supporting defense acquisition, program management, submarine, shipbuilding, manufacturing, or related industries.
  • Minimum five (5) years of experience supporting Foreign Military Sales (FMS) programs.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Export Administration Regulations (EAR), AUKUS-related defense initiatives, and other applicable export control regulations.
  • Experience supporting the execution of complex international defense programs, including schedules, budgets, risk management, stakeholder coordination, and program reporting.
