The Technology organization enables and accelerates the company’s growth strategies, delivering global capabilities and services in support of Amex’s customers and colleagues, while maintaining 24/7 servicing and availability to ensure an uninterrupted, high-quality customer experience. Technology provides the foundation for everything we do in the company while driving differentiation through building and leveraging innovative technology and data insights.

At American Express, our mission is to deliver the world’s best customer experience every day. At the heart of this mission is our Information Security organization, enabling exceptional experiences built on a foundation of trust, service, and security. We leverage advanced technologies and data-driven insights to stay ahead of an evolving threat landscape. We foster a culture of passion, curiosity, and courage—empowering you to innovate, grow, and help shape the future of a Fortune 100 company.

Trust. Service. Security.

The Data Security team is responsible for safeguarding the organization’s most critical asset—its data—by ensuring confidentiality, integrity, and availability across all platforms and environments. Working at the intersection of cybersecurity, data governance, and privacy, the Data Security team focuses on capabilities such as data classification, encryption, secure data access, and monitoring. The team partners closely with engineering, risk, and business units to embed security controls throughout the data lifecycle—from creation and storage to sharing and archival.

This roles leads the design and modernization of enterprise cryptographic architecture, translating Data Security standards and emerging cryptographic requirements into implementable, reusable and increasingly automated security capabilities.

Provides technical leadership across payment and non-payment encryption, key management and HSMs, certificate and PKI architecture, cloud cryptography, post-quantum readiness and crypto-agility, and emerging cryptographic technologies including blockchain and distributed-ledger use cases.

The successful candidate will combine deep cryptographic expertise with strong engineering capability, moving beyond traditional architecture documentation to create architecture-as-code, reusable patterns, reference implementations, APIs and automated security guardrails that engineering teams can directly consume.

  • Define enterprise cryptographic architecture and strategic patterns across payment and non-payment environments, applications, APIs, databases, cloud platforms and infrastructure.

  • Lead post-quantum cryptography readiness and crypto-agility, including cryptographic inventory and CBOM, identification of quantum-vulnerable implementations, migration patterns and modernization roadmaps.

  • Provide architecture leadership for payment cryptography, including payment HSMs, payment key management, cryptographic key hierarchies and applicable PCI requirements.

  • Design modern approaches for enterprise encryption, key management, HSM/HSMaaS, PKI and certificates, digital signatures and cloud-native cryptography.

  • Evaluate emerging cryptographic technologies and use cases, including blockchain and distributed ledgers, advanced digital-signature approaches and other modern cryptographic techniques.

  • Translate Data Security standards into architecture-as-code, reusable engineering patterns, reference implementations, APIs and automated guardrails.

  • Partner directly with engineering teams to prototype, validate and implement cryptographic solutions rather than relying solely on architecture documentation.

  • Integrate cryptographic requirements and security telemetry into the SDLC and Permit to Operate, enabling earlier identification and enforcement of security requirements.

  • Drive adoption of strategic enterprise cryptographic services and identify opportunities to simplify or retire fragmented and legacy implementations.

  • Assess cryptographic risk based on algorithm strength, key protection, data sensitivity, threat exposure, implementation architecture and evolving industry standards.

  • Provide senior technical leadership for significant cryptographic vulnerabilities, incidents, architecture decisions and technology transformations.

  • Mentor architects and engineers and raise cryptographic engineering capability across the organization.

  • Significant experience in cryptographic engineering, cybersecurity architecture, applied cryptography or security engineering in a large-scale technology environment.

  • Deep knowledge of symmetric and asymmetric cryptography, encryption, digital signatures, hashing, TLS, key establishment and exchange, and modern cryptographic protocols.

  • Strong experience with HSMs, enterprise key-management systems, PKI, certificates and cryptographic key lifecycle management.

  • Experience designing encryption solutions across applications, APIs, databases, infrastructure and cloud environments.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate security requirements into working technical architectures and reusable engineering patterns.

  • Software engineering or automation capability sufficient to develop prototypes, integrations, policy or architecture-as-code and technical reference implementations.

  • Experience working across engineering, architecture, product and cybersecurity organizations.

  • Ability to communicate complex cryptographic concepts, risks and architecture decisions to engineering teams and senior leadership.

  • Post-quantum cryptography (PQC), NIST PQC standards and enterprise crypto-agility programs.

  • Experience within financial services or another highly regulated environment.

  • Cloud KMS and HSM architectures across AWS, Azure and/or GCP.

  • Large-scale cryptographic migrations or modernization programs.

  • Payment cryptography, payment HSMs, payment key management and PCI requirements.

Highly Desired Experience

  1. Cryptographic inventory and Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM) capabilities.

  2. Blockchain and distributed-ledger cryptography and associated key and signature architectures.

  3. DevSecOps, architecture-as-code, policy-as-code and automated SDLC security enforcement.

What Makes This Role Different

This is not a traditional architecture role centered on reviewing designs and producing documentation.

The role is expected to turn cryptographic strategy and standards into capabilities that engineers can implement: Standards -> Architecture -> Code and Patterns -> Enterprise Services -> Automated Assurance.

Success means making secure cryptography easier, faster and more consistent to implement while preparing the enterprise for major transitions such as post-quantum cryptography. Hands-on engineering capability is strongly preferred.

title: Payment Reference Matching Clerk
description:
Payment Reference Matching Clerk

Office Administration · Billing Records · Remote · Full-time or part-time
Pay: £25.25–£27.25 an hour

Not every payment arrives with an immediately recognisable reference. In this role, you would help a billing team identify routine matches between a supplied payment detail and an existing account record.

The purpose is to make information ready for the person responsible for the account, not to post unauthorised financial adjustments. You would use an online system, compare straightforward details and flag anything that cannot be linked with confidence.

The work starts with a source record: perhaps a payment notification, a transaction reference or a customer’s message about a payment. You would check the details against the record the employer makes available, following a defined sequence. A matching reference and amount may allow a routine note or handoff under the company’s process. An amount that differs, an account with several possible matches or a message lacking identifying information calls for clarification. You would record what you checked instead of forcing a match to make the queue look complete.

A small difference can change the result

Imagine an email that gives the last digits of a reference and a payment date. You find one likely account but another payment on the same date has a similar amount. The correct next step is to ask for more information or send the item to a billing colleague. It is not to choose the most convenient match. Conversely, when the exact reference is present and the team’s checklist allows it, you can complete the assigned record update efficiently and leave a concise note. The job rewards dependable comparisons rather than investigative flair.

The clerk does not make decisions about refunds, credit, arrears or a customer’s entitlement to a service. Those matters have financial consequences and sit with authorised staff. You would also avoid giving a customer a definitive payment-status answer unless the relevant team has confirmed it. A factual acknowledgement that a question has been received is different from a claim that funds have been applied to an account.

There is a difference between a payment reference being present and a payment being correctly assigned. A notification might contain a reference that belongs to an earlier transaction, or a customer may type a number incorrectly. You would check the source that the team designates, document the discrepancy and leave the item for review. Your note should allow a colleague to see which fields agreed and which did not, without requiring them to reconstruct your entire search. It is better to leave an item openly unresolved than to create confidence the records do not support.

Your work may cover:

  • Reading assigned payment-related notifications and extracting the supplied reference.
  • Comparing that reference with the relevant account or invoice record.
  • Checking a date and amount where the written process calls for it.
  • Identifying a possible duplicate notification before creating a second entry.
  • Recording a permitted match with a clear source note.
  • Leaving an unmatched item visibly pending rather than choosing an uncertain account.
  • Asking for a missing detail through the approved channel.
  • Passing discrepancies and adjustment requests to the billing colleague.

You can learn the employer’s system through training. Prior billing or office administrative experience is helpful but not required. Applicants at the start of their careers are welcome if they can work accurately with numbers, read a short procedure and say when two records do not clearly agree. Basic spreadsheet familiarity may help, but a specialised accounting qualification is unnecessary. Customer service skills are useful for a courteous request for missing information, though most of the work is record-based.

As a remote worker, you would keep your queue and notes current so a colleague can see which items have been matched, questioned or referred. A home office space suited to careful computer work can support that attention. You should handle account details only through the employer’s approved online systems. The team will explain its escalation route and which updates you may enter yourself.

Rate and arrangement

£25.25–£27.25 per hour, with full-time or part-time hours according to the opening. The role is a junior support position, centred on routine comparison and accurate handoff rather than accounting judgement.

Application

Evidence of careful numerical checking is more useful here than a finance-sounding job title. Perhaps you compared receipts, entered references or kept a simple record in another setting.

New applicants can learn the billing system; the first step is to show basic accuracy and a willingness to ask when a match is uncertain. If you’re selected for the next step, you may be asked to complete an application on the hiring company’s website. Your initial application should make any such practical experience easy to identify.

title: Senior Core Infrastructure Engineer
description:
Designs, implements, and optimizes components in distributed systems with an emphasis on scalability, resiliency, and operability. Delivers features and load/performance tests; leverages data plane platforms and distributed state tools for high-volume retrieval, storage, and processing; and reviews peers’ implementations for scalability compliance. Builds fault-tolerant paths (redundancy, replication, automatic failover), applies recovery‑oriented principles, and implements retries, circuit breakers, and timeouts. Proactively detects and mitigates issues via tests, alarms, dashboards, and telemetry; authors runbooks and participates in incident response and RCAs. Implements standard replication and synchronization, develops automation/IaC for troubleshooting and maintenance, and applies advanced security controls (encryption, access, remediation) while ensuring change, compliance, and documentation standards are met.

Key Responsibilities
System Design & Architecture - System Scalability:
–Implements and contributes to the development for components of distributed systems that support horizontal and vertical scaling including leveraging distributed state management tools.
–Optimizes code and/or systems for large-scale data processing in large-scale systems.
–Implements scalability requirements for assigned components and reviews implementation of team members.
–Leverages components of data plane platforms to handle large-scale data retrieval, storage, and processing.
–Implements performance and load testing.
System Design & Architecture - System Reliability Design:
–Collaborates with team to build fault-tolerant components capable of withstanding in-service updates by implementing redundancy, replication, and automatic failover mechanisms.
–Applies recovery oriented computing principles to design components that effectively handle service disruptions.
–Implements retry mechanisms, circuit breakers, and timeouts to help handle network unreliability.
System Design & Architecture - System Reliability Performance:
–Implements tests and alarm configurations to proactively detect and address issues/failures.
–Supports efforts to recover from failures by drafting and executing runbooks and operational procedures.
–Builds and customizes dashboards, telemetry systems, and alerting mechanisms to monitor component health.
System Design & Architecture - Correctness / Availability:
–Designs and implements functional requirements and testing for assigned features within an existing system.
–Implements tests scenarios (e.g., fault-injection, brown-out) to evaluate system correctness.
–Implements standard data replication and synchronization techniques to maintain data integrity and availability.
Operational Troubleshooting & Incident Management:
–Diagnoses, debugs, and resolves issues in system components to support ongoing operation.
–Implements basic strategies to prevent interruptions, ensuring no maintenance windows are required for customers and users when resolving issues.
–Designs and implements automation scripts and tooling used to troubleshoot operational issues.
–Participates in operational support rotations, assisting in incident responses and root cause investigations.
Compliance & Security:
–Applies advanced security measures to protect data and applications in multi-tenant environments, including encryption and access controls.
–Implements remediation plans to continuously improve security.
–Collaborates with the team to ensure cloud infrastructure complies with relevant industry standards and regulations and that documentation is up-to-date
Automation & Change Management:
–Maintains automation scripts and tools (e.g., Infrastructure as Code (IaC)) for managing cloud infrastructure.
–Adheres to change management plans for patching, updating, and rolling back applications.


Core Responsibilities
Planning & Execution:
–Track timelines with minimal supervision, ensuring work is completed in a timely manner and is in alignment with project requirements.
–Prioritize and adjust work as resources or timelines change, with some guidance
Collaboration & Partnership:
–Collaborates across teams to align on expectations and achieve shared objectives. Builds and maintains a comprehensive understanding of business, stakeholder, and/or customer needs to build and support effective partnerships. Actively listens to diverse perspectives and asks questions to ensure understanding of others.
Problem Solving:
–Independently identifies and addresses standard and non-standard issues in accordance with standard practices, escalating more complex issues as appropriate. Analyzes data and/or information from multiple sources to troubleshoot standard and non-standard errors. Contributes to knowledge sharing and best practices
Continuous Learning:
–Embraces continuous learning by actively seeking to build knowledge and new skills and/or tools, and staying current with industry trends and best practices. Seeks out and leverages feedback and training to improve skills. Contributes to a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing with team members..
Continuous Improvement:
–Develops ideas and recommends updates to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows within a team. Seeks input from team members on alternative approaches and methods for improving work.

title: Sr Data Engineer
description:
Optum is a global organization that delivers care, aided by technology to help millions of people live healthier lives. The work you do with our team will directly improve health outcomes by connecting people with the care, pharmacy benefits, and data they need to feel their best. Here, you will find a culture guided by diversity and inclusion, talented peers, comprehensive benefits, and career development opportunities. As a Senior Data Engineer on the UHC Core Data KTLO team, you will join our dynamic technology organization in Eden Prairie, MN, dedicated to building and optimizing robust data pipelines and systems that power critical healthcare platforms. In this role, you will design and deliver modern data and AI-powered solutions, platforms, and automations for enterprise scale. You will work with state-of-the-art technologies such as Python, Spark, Scala, and Kafka to build scalable, high-performance data processing pipelines and apply data warehousing and modeling best practices. You will play a key role in driving innovation by identifying opportunities to streamline workflows, automate tasks, and leverage advanced tools to address complex business challenges. Focus on KTLO activities, including vulnerability remediation, tool and version upgrades, data security, and platform stability. Additionally, support Azure Data Factory pipelines, Databricks workloads, and cloud components such as Blob Storage and AzCopy.

You'll enjoy the flexibility to telecommute* from anywhere within the U.S. as you take on some tough challenges.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and deploy AI-powered solutions to address complex business challenges with emphasis on responsible use of AI
  • Evaluate emerging trends to inform solution design and strategic innovation
  • Use enterprise-approved AI tools to streamline workflows, automate tasks, and drive continuous improvement
  • Build, optimize, and maintain robust, scalable data pipelines and processes using Python, Spark, and Scala

  • Apply and promote data warehousing, data modeling, and database design best practices
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand data requirements and translate them into high-performing technical solutions
  • Identify and implement performance tuning and query optimization across large-scale datasets
  • Design, develop, and deploy AI-powered solutions to address complex business challenges with emphasis on responsible use of AI

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

Required Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in data engineering, software engineering, or related field
  • 3+ years of experience building and optimizing data processes and pipelines using Python, SQL,Spark, and Scala
  • 3+ years of experience with data warehousing, dimensional data modeling, and database design
  • 2+ years of experience supporting streaming data architectures and messaging platforms with Apache Kafka
  • 2+ years of experience designing and deploying scalable automated solutions, platforms, or workflows (including integration of automation tools)
  • 1+ years of experience with Apache Airflow for workflow orchestration, scheduling, and monitoring of data pipelines

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, or a related field
  • Experience working with cloud data platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, or Snowflake)
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines, containerization (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes), and version control (Git)
  • Experience evaluating emerging technology trends and applying modern automation tools to streamline engineering workflows
  • Experience with relational and NoSQL databases
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a track record of applying responsible design standards
  • Familiarity with IBM DataStage for legacy ETL development and integration with enterprise data platforms
  • Experience working with healthcare data and understanding of compliance, regulatory, and data privacy standards
  • Hands-on experience with Teradata for large-scale data warehousing, query optimization, and performance tuning
  • Proficiency in Unix/Linux environments with scripting capabilities for automation and operational support

*All Telecommuters will be required to adhere to UnitedHealth Group's Telecommuter Policy.

Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets, education, work experience, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, we offer benefits such as, a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). No matter where or when you begin a career with us, you'll find a far-reaching choice of benefits and incentives. The salary for this role will range from $91,700 to $163,700 annually based on full-time employment. We comply with all minimum wage laws as applicable.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

title: Quality Assurance Manager
description:
Own the Quality: Quality Assurance Manager

This role goes beyond inspections. It’s about protecting standards, elevating construction quality, and ensuring every home is built right.

At Stylecraft, we don’t just build homes—we build trust, strong communities, and lasting relationships. For nearly 40 years, we’ve helped Texans achieve the American Dream, and we’re proud to be recognized as one of the Best Places to Work in Texas year after year.

We’re looking for a Quality Assurance Manager who’s detail-driven, field-focused, and ready to make a real impact on how our communities are built.
Why This Role Is Different
This position sits at the intersection of construction quality, field operations, and continuous improvement. You won’t just check work—you’ll influence how it gets done.

What sets this role apart:
  • You’re the Standard Setter: You help ensure every home meets Stylecraft quality standards before it ever reaches a homeowner.
  • Field Over Desk: Spend the majority of your time in the field performing inspections and working alongside construction teams.
  • Real Impact: Your feedback drives improvements in materials, processes, and long-term build quality.
  • Collaborative Influence: Work closely with construction teams, trade partners, and leadership to uphold excellence across multifamily projects.
  • A Company That Invests in You: We support your growth, value your expertise, and trust your judgment.
The Details
  • Role: Quality Assurance Manager
  • Location: In-Person / Field-Based
  • Schedule: Monday–Friday
  • Type: Full-Time
  • Pay: $50,000 - $54,000
What Your Day Looks Like
You’re the eyes and ears of quality across our builds—ensuring every phase meets expectations and standards.
  • Field Inspections: Conduct pre-drywall, final, and completion inspections on multifamily homes and townhomes.
  • Quality Assurance: Ensure all work meets Stylecraft standards, building codes, and best practices.
  • Collaboration: Partner with construction teams and trade contractors to explain expectations and resolve issues efficiently.
  • Continuous Improvement: Identify trends, provide feedback, and help refine QA standards and processes.
  • Technical Support: Guide trade partners on installation methods and quality expectations.
  • Data & Reporting: Document inspection results and maintain organized, accurate reports.
  • Travel: Visit job sites across Central, South, and East Texas as needed.
Are You the Right Fit?
We’re not looking for someone who just checks boxes—you’ll thrive here if:
  • You have strong attention to detail and hold a high bar for quality
  • You’re confident communicating with construction teams and trade partners
  • You take ownership and proactively solve problems
  • You’re comfortable working in the field and managing multiple priorities
  • You have a valid driver’s license and are open to travel as needed
What You Bring
  • Experience in residential construction, inspections, or quality assurance
  • Knowledge of building codes and construction processes
  • Multifamily or townhome experience preferred
  • Strong communication and organizational skills
  • Technical understanding of construction systems (water intrusion, materials, etc.)
Your Mindset Aligns With Our Core Values
  • Care: Take ownership and go the extra mile
  • Serve: Turn challenges into opportunities to deliver excellence
  • Improve: Always look for ways to raise the bar

title: Sr Software Engineer II
description:

The Technology organization enables and accelerates the company’s growth strategies, delivering global capabilities and services in support of Amex’s customers and colleagues, while maintaining 24/7 servicing and availability to ensure an uninterrupted, high-quality customer experience. Technology provides the foundation for everything we do in the company while driving differentiation through building and leveraging innovative technology and data insights.

The Enterprise CRM Solutions team was created as part of the company’s Framework for Winning, with a mission to reimagine the platform and solution-delivery model to improve strategic agility, speed to market, effectiveness of delivery, and transparency. The Enterprise Customer Relationship Management Solutions (ECRMS) team develops capabilities for the Sales and Customer domains, harnessing Data-GCP, SAAS, Machine Learning, and Artificial Intelligence to enable powerful selling and re-selling experiences, acquire new customers, and deepen existing client relationships.

We are seeking a highly experienced Senior Engineer – CRM, Data & Cloud Platforms to help architect and build the next generation of enterprise CRM capabilities.

This is a hands-on senior engineering role at the intersection of Salesforce, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), data engineering, APIs, distributed systems, and data security. The engineer will design and develop secure, scalable, resilient, and observable solutions that connect Salesforce with enterprise data platforms and enable trusted data to be accessed and consumed across CRM, analytics, ML, and AI use cases.

The ideal candidate brings deep software engineering expertise and approaches data and APIs as products—creating reusable, well-governed capabilities with clear contracts, ownership, documentation, security, quality, discoverability, reliability, and service-level expectations.

  • Design and build end-to-end enterprise CRM capabilities spanning Salesforce, GCP, APIs, and enterprise data platforms, from customer-facing CRM experiences through the underlying data and integration layers.
  • Develop scalable solutions on Salesforce, applying strong knowledge of Salesforce data architecture, Apex, APIs, integration patterns, platform capabilities, and SaaS application development.
  • Engineer high-volume data pipelines and processing capabilities on GCP using BigQuery, Bigtable, Dataflow, Dataproc/Spark, Pub/Sub, Cloud Composer/Airflow, Cloud Storage, and related technologies.
  • Design the data connectivity between Salesforce and enterprise data ecosystems, using APIs, events, streaming, CDC, batch integration, federation, and virtualization based on the needs of the use case.
  • Own data modeling and management across Salesforce and GCP, including data quality, metadata, lineage, lifecycle management, reconciliation, and governance.
  • Design for data security and accessibility across both platforms, including Salesforce sharing and access models, GCP IAM, authentication/authorization, encryption, tokenization, masking, and least-privilege access.
  • Build data virtualization and federation patterns that make enterprise data available to CRM experiences without unnecessarily replicating or moving large volumes of data.
  • Design and build secure, reliable APIs and integration services, with well-defined contracts, documentation, versioning, lifecycle management, authentication/authorization, and governance.
  • Build event-driven architectures using Salesforce Platform Events/CDC, Pub/Sub, Kafka, or similar technologies to support real-time and asynchronous data flows.
  • Engineer for reliability and observability across Salesforce, APIs, events, and data pipelines through logging, metrics, tracing, alerting, SLIs/SLOs, retries, idempotency, and resilient failure handling.
  • Drive a Data as a Product mindset by creating trusted, reusable, discoverable data products and services with clear ownership, contracts, quality standards, security, and service expectations.
  • Optimize solutions for scale, performance, reliability, and cost, particularly for large-volume Salesforce and GCP data workloads.

The Quantitative Biosciences Institute (QBI) at UCSF brings together researchers across the biomedical, physical, and computational sciences to address complex problems in biology and human disease. QBI supports large, multi-investigator programs that integrate quantitative proteomics, structural biology, genetics, and advanced computational and AI methods, and works extensively with academic, government, and industry partners in the United States and internationally. Based at Byers Hall on the UCSF Mission Bay campus, QBI provides a highly collaborative, interdisciplinary environment in which computational scientists work directly alongside experimental groups to translate large-scale biological data into mechanistic understanding and therapeutic hypotheses.

title: Senior Analytics Engineer
description:
Our Story:
Crisis Prevention Institute, Inc. (CPI) is the worldwide leader in evidence‑based de‑escalation and crisis prevention training and dementia care services. Our programs teach professionals the skills to recognize, prevent, and respond to crises in the workplace. Since 1980, we’ve helped train more than 17 million people across service‑oriented industries including education, health care, behavioral health, long‑term care, human services, security, corporate, and retail.
At CPI, we are dedicated to changing behaviors and reducing conflict for the Care, Welfare, Safety, and Security of everyone. We believe empathy, meaningful connections, personal safety, and security are the antidotes to fear and anxiety. This philosophy is central to everything we do and traces back to our beginning.

As a member of the team, you can expect to:
  • Make a difference through your work — You’ll be proud to tell your family and friends what you do.
  • Gain significant career experience within a fast‑growing organization — From entry‑level roles to executive leadership.
  • Feel fulfilled and have fun — We work hard but make time to build meaningful relationships and celebrate wins.
The Role:
The Senior Analytics Engineer is a business-facing solution owner responsible for translating complex business needs into trusted, scalable data and analytics solutions. Working as a forward-deployed partner within the business, this role owns solutions from discovery and design through delivery, adoption, and continuous improvement. The position enables reporting, business intelligence, analytics, and AI use cases; curates reusable semantic models; integrates governed data into AI-enabled solutions; and advances practical data governance. The role works across a modern cloud data stack—including Snowflake, Power BI, and Fivetran—while partnering closely with business and technology stakeholders to deliver measurable outcomes.

What You Get to Do Every Day:
  • Serve as the end-to-end owner for assigned data and analytics solutions, from business discovery and requirements through design, delivery, adoption, support, and continuous improvement.
  • Embed with business teams as a consultative, forward-deployed engineering partner to understand workflows, frame problems, recommend solutions, and deliver measurable business outcomes.
  • Design, build, test, deploy, and maintain reporting, dashboarding, business intelligence, and analytics solutions, primarily using Power BI and complementary AI-enabled tools.
  • Curate analytics-ready datasets and design, build, and maintain governed semantic layers—including reusable semantic models, shared measures, business definitions, and metadata—that provide consistent, trusted data for self-service analytics, reporting, and AI-enabled solutions.
  • Develop and optimize data transformations and integrations across Snowflake, Fivetran, Power BI, and other components of the modern cloud data stack.
  • Partner with AI project teams to prepare, integrate, and operationalize trusted enterprise data for AI-assisted workflows, search, automation, and analytical use cases.
  • Apply data governance standards in daily delivery, including ownership, definitions, lineage, access, privacy, quality, documentation, and lifecycle management.
  • Establish validation, monitoring, and support practices that ensure solutions are accurate, reliable, secure, performant, and usable.
  • Communicate technical concepts clearly to nontechnical audiences; facilitate tradeoff decisions; and provide training, documentation, and change support that drive adoption.
  • Contribute reusable patterns, peer reviews, mentoring, and engineering standards while maintaining primary accountability for the success of assigned business solutions.
You Need to Have:
  • Bachelor’s degree
  • At least six years of progressive experience in analytics engineering, business intelligence, data engineering, data analytics, or a closely related field, including demonstrated ownership of production data and analytics solutions.
  • Experience partnering directly with business stakeholders to discover needs, design solutions, deliver value, and support adoption
  • Hands-on experience delivering solutions on a modern cloud data platform and business intelligence stack.
  • Advanced SQL and strong knowledge of data modeling, transformation, testing, performance optimization, and analytics engineering practices.
  • Strong Power BI capabilities, including semantic modeling, DAX, Power Query, report development, deployment, governance, and performance tuning.
  • Working knowledge of cloud data warehouses, ingestion and transformation patterns, version control, release practices, and production support.
  • Ability to translate ambiguous business questions into well-scoped, durable technical solutions and to balance speed, usability, scalability, governance, and maintainability.
  • Strong facilitation, consulting, communication, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence decisions across technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Demonstrated accountability, sound judgment, curiosity, and a product-oriented mindset focused on business value and user adoption.
  • Ability to work independently across multiple priorities while collaborating effectively with business partners, data professionals, application teams, security, and AI teams.


We’d Love to See:
  • Experience with Snowflake, Power BI, and Fivetran, or comparable tools within a modern cloud data ecosystem.
  • Experience designing and building enterprise semantic layers, including reusable semantic models, governed metrics, shared business definitions, and self-service analytics capabilities.
  • Experience enabling AI, machine learning, natural-language analytics, or automation use cases with trusted enterprise data.
  • Experience with dimensional modeling, data quality, metadata, lineage, access controls, and other applied data governance practices.
  • Relevant cloud, data platform, or Power BI certifications are beneficial but not required.

  • Comprehensive benefits package

  • Health & Wellness Days

  • Continuing education and training
  • Hybrid / Remote work schedule

title: Summer Test Administrator and Proctor
description:

title: Research Data Analyst I
description:
Job Function Summary

Involves gathering, analyzing, and interpreting a wide variety of research data. Designs and conducts research including selecting data samples, developing research instruments, analyzing collected information according to established statistical methods, and developing recommendations based on research findings. Prepares reports, charts, tables, and other visual aids to interpret and communicate data and results.

Generic Scope

Entry-level professional with limited prior experience; learns to use professional concepts to resolve problems of limited scope and complexity; works on assignments that are initially routine in nature, requiring limited judgment and decision making. Employees at this level are expected to acquire the skills and knowledge to perform more advanced work following an agreed upon time in position, through defined training and development planning.

Custom Scope

Under direct supervision, acquires skills and knowledge of professional concepts in research data analysis. Works on small projects or segments of projects with limited scope and complexity.

Department Overview

The Department of Radiology & Biomedical Imaging is one of the largest departments within the School of Medicine, generating more than $40 million in professional fee revenues each year, and submitting grant proposals resulting in $30-40 million of awards each year. More than 90% of the MD faculty in Radiology is based at the Parnassus Campus, including nine of the ten clinical sections and their chiefs, and five of the seven vice chairs. The department has significant clinical and research operations at China Basin, Mission Bay, the VAMC, ZSFG, and Mount Zion. It includes more than 150 academic personnel and approximately 225 staff FTE. In addition, there are more than 90 resident, fellow, and graduate student trainees.

The Research Data Anl 1 position is focused on the collection of clinical data focused on patients treated with PSMA radioligand therapy and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy. A multicenter database is being created to collect data on these patients to understand toxicity, efficacy and see how these drugs are used clinically. The candidate will work under the general supervision and guidance from the supervisor Dr. Thomas Hope. They will also work with Dr. Abuzar Tuchayi Moradi.

Statistical and Data Analysis

  • Under direct supervision, performs basic statistical and data analysis.

Research Data Collection and Preparation

Collects research data and prepares it for analysis.

  • Entering clinical data from the medical record system into the REDcap database.
  • Interpreting imaging reports and converting them to binary data entry format.
  • Determining progressing free survival dates based on imaging and reports.

Study Design

  • Assists with study design proposals and survey instruments.

Report Preparation and Analysis

Assists with report preparation and / or analysis for internal constituents.

  • Reviewing pathology reports and determining appropriate Ki-67 and other variables.

Clinical Data Storage and Documentation

Develops knowledge in areas of storage, documentation and dissemination of computerized data.

  • Collect data on patients to understand toxicity, efficacy and see how these drugs are used clinically.
  • Collection of clinical data focused on patients treated with PSMA radioligand therapy and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
  • Acquiring knowledge of research function. Acquiring ability to perform research analysis duties.
  • Acquiring statistical analysis, systems programming, and database design skills to perform research analysis duties.
  • Ability to effectively manage time and see assigned parts of projects through to completion on deadline.
  • Basic consultation and communication skills.
  • Attention to Details.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous exposure to Medical Care.

Licenses

None listed.

Certifications

None listed.

title: Senior AI Engineer II - Forward Deployed Engineer - Enterprise AI Platforms
description:
Why Join American Express

Joining Amex Tech means discovering and shaping your contribution to something big. Here, you can work alongside talented tech teams and build a unique career with the Powerful Backing of American Express. Technology provides the foundation for everything we do in the company while driving differentiation through building and leveraging innovative technology and data insights.

The Enterprise AI Platform organization partners with business and technology teams to shape the Enterprise AI strategy, bring emerging technologies to the forefront, and build scalable, reusable AI platforms. This team plays a pivotal role in enabling American Express to operate as an AI-powered enterprise by equipping teams with the skills, platforms, and seamless deployment capabilities needed to accelerate responsible AI innovation, enhance decision-making, and drive customer impact with speed and scale.

Join a team shaping the future of AI at American Express. You will work directly with business and product leaders to turn high-value opportunities into trusted, secure, and responsible AI solutions, while helping successful ideas become reusable capabilities across the enterprise.

FDE partners across American Express to transform high-value business opportunities into trusted, secure, and scalable AI solutions delivering measurable outcomes, accelerating adoption, and turning successful innovations into reusable enterprise capabilities.

Role Summary

As a Forward Deployed AI Engineer, you will partner closely with business units, product teams, and engineering organizations to identify and reframe high-value opportunities, translate business challenges into clear value propositions, and build working solutions using Generative AI, agentic systems, and intelligent automation.

You will take opportunities from discovery and demonstration through proof of value, production scaling, adoption, and transition to long-term ownership. Demonstrations are a means of validating grounded value propositions, not the end goal. You will be accountable for advancing credible opportunities into real adoption and durable ways of working, with each stage tied to measurable outcomes and balanced with enterprise requirements for security, reliability, and responsible AI.

This is a hands-on engineering role with a significant stakeholder engagement component. You will influence without direct authority, communicate across levels of seniority and technical familiarity, and work alongside engineers to build and deploy reliable software.

You will challenge assumptions about how work is performed, analyze processes as systems, and identify the technical, operational, and organizational levers that can improve them. You will define a longer-term direction while sequencing practical near-term solutions that build toward it.

Candidates may come from mobile, web, backend, distributed-systems, or workflow-platform backgrounds. What matters most is the ability to understand a system end to end, form a point of view, engage deeply with users, and turn direction into working software.

Opportunity discovery and transformation

  • Build trusted relationships and develop a deep understanding of business priorities, user needs, operational workflows, and sources of friction.
  • Challenge existing assumptions, map processes as systems, and identify the technical, operational, and organizational changes most likely to improve them.
  • Lead discovery sessions that translate business needs into clear use cases, value propositions, measurable success criteria, and solution direction.
  • Assess opportunities based on business value, technical feasibility, user impact, risk, and readiness for adoption.
  • Define a longer-term vision and identify the smallest useful intervention that can validate the opportunity while preserving a path to broader transformation.

Solution design and delivery

  • Design, build, and deploy Generative AI, agentic AI, and intelligent automation solutions using approved enterprise platform capabilities.
  • Develop working demonstrations and proofs of value that test assumptions and measure business impact.
  • Take solutions through prototyping, production scaling, adoption, and transition to long-term ownership.
  • Build agents and AI-enabled workflows that interact with enterprise APIs, knowledge sources, data platforms, applications, code, and business processes.
  • Incorporate appropriate human input, approval, escalation, and fallback mechanisms.
  • Work directly alongside engineering teams to produce software and apply the architecture, testing, deployment, and operational practices required for production use.
  • Use experimentation selectively to reduce uncertainty while balancing speed with security, reliability, maintainability, and governance.

AI-enabled engineering practices

  • Use coding agents and AI-assisted engineering techniques to accelerate discovery, implementation, testing, documentation, and iteration.
  • Apply specification-driven development, context management, iterative planning, and structured knowledge repositories to preserve context and improve personal productivity.
  • Evaluate agent-generated code and technical outputs for correctness, security, maintainability, and architectural alignment.
  • Identify where AI-enabled development practices can improve engineering throughput without compromising operational standards.

Platform contribution and scale

  • Generalize patterns and components developed through individual engagements for broader use.
  • Partner with platform and product teams to turn successful prototypes into reusable features, accelerators, reference architectures, and paved-road implementation patterns.
  • Capture lessons from deployments and use them to influence the enterprise AI platform and product roadmap.
  • Help teams adopt AI-enabled workflows and transition solutions into sustainable operating models.

Evaluation, governance, and responsible AI

  • Develop evaluation approaches that measure solution quality, task completion, business outcomes, user experience, latency, cost, and reliability.
  • Identify and address failure modes through testing, monitoring, safeguards, and iterative improvement.
  • Ensure solutions meet American Express requirements for security, privacy, risk management, responsible AI, and regulatory compliance.
  • Establish appropriate controls for model access, enterprise data, tool use, human oversight, and production operations.

Stakeholder leadership

  • Communicate technical concepts, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to audiences with different levels of technical familiarity and seniority.
  • Influence decisions and drive alignment across business, product, engineering, risk, and platform teams without relying on direct reporting authority.
  • Maintain strong stakeholder relationships throughout discovery, delivery, adoption, and transition, and mentor partner teams on AI solution delivery.
  • 5 or more years of experience delivering software, technical solutions, or digital products in an engineering, architecture, or technical consulting capacity.
  • Demonstrated ability to take an ambiguous business or user problem through discovery, implementation, and measurable validation.
  • Experience using coding agents in a structured engineering workflow, including specification-driven development, context management, iterative implementation, and reusable knowledge repositories.
  • Software engineering fluency and the ability to contribute directly to applications, integrations, services, or technical prototypes.
  • Experience in at least one relevant domain, such as mobile, web, backend services, APIs, distributed systems, platform engineering, workflow orchestration, or cloud-native development.
  • Ability to reason about systems end to end, identify constraints and leverage points, and connect technical decisions to business outcomes.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-partnership skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts, challenge existing approaches constructively, and influence without direct authority.
  • Ability to define a longer-term direction and sequence incremental solutions that build toward it.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building or deploying solutions powered by language models, agentic systems, or AI-enabled process flows.
  • Experience with retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases, tool calling, model context protocols, knowledge retrieval, or workflow technologies such as Temporal, LangGraph, LangChain, or LlamaIndex.
  • Experience designing human-in-the-loop controls and operational safeguards, with knowledge of AI evaluation, observability, and responsible AI.
  • Experience supporting technology adoption or operating-model transformation, particularly in financial services or another regulated industry.

Success Measures

Success in this role will be measured by:

  • AI opportunities that progress from discovery to proof of value and, where appropriate, production adoption.
  • Measurable business outcomes tied to clearly defined KPIs.
  • Ability to identify and reframe valuable opportunities while connecting near-term delivery to longer-term transformation.
  • Solutions that improve the broader workflow and are adopted into sustainable operating models.
  • Strong stakeholder relationships, technical quality, and effective management of security, risk, and reliability.
  • Reusable capabilities and implementation patterns incorporated into the enterprise AI platform.

Working Model and Travel

Occasional travel may be required for workshops or key delivery milestones, but frequent travel is not expected. Roles may be based near selected American Express offices to support close partnerships with regional business and product teams.

title: Senior Model Validation Quant
description:
**Job Description

**Are you an engineer with a solid quantitative foundation, or a quantitative analyst with interest in modern software development and engineering discipline? Join Credit Risk Model Validation at Danske Bank and help us build the most technologically advanced, automated credit model risk management department in the Nordics.

In Credit Risk Model Validation (CRMV), we are reimagining how model risk is managed across Danske Bank. We are moving away from manual data wrangling, ad-hoc scripts, and copied notebooks towards an industrialised, reproducible, and AI-accelerated quantitative engineering ecosystem. In this role you will bridge the traditional divide between quantitative model validation and software engineering, with your initial focus being roughly 70% tooling and infrastructure engineering and 30% direct model validation.

You will be part of a collaborative, forward-thinking team operating on a modern stack: migrating to GitHub Enterprise Cloud and Databricks, building modular internal Python packages, configuring Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs), setting up GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows, and embedding GitHub Copilot as a standard daily partner in engineering.

This position can be located in Vilnius, Lithuania or Copenhagen, Denmark. The relocation package isn't applicable for this role.

**What You Will Be Doing

**

  • Build and evolve validation software: design, implement, and maintain core Python packages and shared libraries that turn complex quantitative methodologies into clean, parameter-driven, and testable tools.
  • Architect modern workflows & infrastructure: set up and manage GitHub Actions workflows, CI/CD pipelines, and Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs) to ensure seamless, automated, and audit-ready execution across environments.
  • Empower and enable the department: create the tooling and automated templates that allow fellow validators to run analyses, generate standard evidence bundles, and produce publication-ready PDF reports with minimal manual friction.
  • Perform and lead model validations: apply your quantitative insight to independently validate credit risk models (such as PD, LGD, CF, IFRS 9, etc.), assessing conceptual soundness, statistical performance, and model limitations.
  • Integrate AI-assisted engineering: make heavy daily use of GitHub Copilot to accelerate code delivery, write thorough test suites, and modernise legacy codebases.
  • Promote engineering excellence: champion version control hygiene, structured code reviews, and reproducible analytical practices across the entire team.
  • Engage key stakeholders: present technical architectures, quantitative findings, and validation conclusions clearly and persuasively to model developers, risk leaders, and regulatory counterparts.

**About You

**

  • Quantitative grounding: you hold an MSc, PhD, or equivalent practical experience in a quantitative discipline (e.g. Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Physics, Quantitative Finance, Data Science, or Engineering).
  • Strong software and coding habits: you have solid hands-on experience writing clean, modular Python and SQL.

title: Staff AI Engineer
description:
About OrbitShift


At OrbitShift, we are building the world's first AI-native Sales Operating System, trusted by enterprise teams to accelerate theirGTMmotion. Our multi-agent AI system enables actionable account insights,RFPresponse generation, targeted nudges, and sales content. Backed by PeakXV(formerly Sequoia Capital), Stellaris Venture Partners, and other marquee investors, we are a fast-growing, 3-year-old startup with a team from Amazon, McKinsey,IIT, and Stanford.

We are looking for aStaff AI Engineerto be our internal authority on applied AI, the person who sets technical direction onwhatwe build with AI, not just how. This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone with staff-level impact in applied AI, backed by solid backend engineering depth.

Role Overview​


You will be our go-to person for everything AI, effectively a Tech Fellow for AI within the org. You'll own the AI technical strategy, translate business problems into AI system designs, decide which models and approaches fit each use case, and own the judgment calls that make GenAI systems reliable and cost-effective in production. Just as importantly, you'll know and argue, whennotto use AI.

This is a hands-on staff-levelICrole with real influence over the AI roadmap and how the whole team builds with AI. You'll pair deep GenAI application experience with solid backend engineering, so your designs hold up in production and not just in a notebook. We care more about depth in fundamentals, scope of impact, and judgment than familiarity with any specific tool.


Requirements

What You'll Do?


Set AI technical direction and strategy

  • Own the AI technical strategy and multi-quarter roadmap across the org , not just execute on individual use cases, but decide where AI creates durable leverage and sequence the bets accordingly.

  • Set the standards, patterns, and guardrails other engineers build against, and establish how the company evaluates, ships, and operates AI quality.

  • Be the internal authority on AI: translate ambiguous business problems into concrete AI system designs, and make the call on approach, including arguing against AI/LLMs when a simpler solution wins.

  • Drive org-level build/buy and model/vendor decisions with real cost and risk stakes; act as the final technical escalation point for hard AI design calls.

  • Select the right model for each use case and balance output quality against cost and latency — routing, prompting strategy, retrieval design, and where fine-tuning is or isn't worth it.

  • Track the field closely, papers, model releases, tooling, and turn what's changed in the last 3–6 months into concrete decisions for us.

Build GenAI systems across the stack

  • Design and build across the GenAI stack, RAG, embeddings and vector stores (e.g., OpenSearch), Agentic architectures, model orchestration and routing (e.g., Amazon Bedrock, OpenRouter), and prompting, with clear opinions on where each approach and framework breaks down.

  • Reason clearly about Agentic flows and long-running, autonomous agents : planning, tool use, memory/state, error recovery, and human-in-the-loop control over extended tasks, as we build agents for our own engineering workflows (including coding agents) and for client-facing use cases.

  • Own production judgment: eval pipelines, observability for LLM and agent systems, guardrails, hallucination mitigation, versioning, and cost control at scale.

Build on solid engineering foundations

  • Bring strong backend and distributed-systems depth to bear, trusted in any architecture review, and able to own the design of the services and data flows the AI features and agents depend on, not just build on top of them (API design, event-driven/async patterns, and the reliability, consistency, and performance trade-offs that come with distributed systems).

  • Operate on a modern cloud and data stack: AWS, containerization, relational databases (PostgreSQL), and solid observability and CI/CD for production services.

Partner across the org and level up the team

  • Work closely with product, design, and the founding team to align on where AI creates real leverage and navigate technical trade-offs.

  • Translate complex AI concepts for non-technical audiences, represent AI direction in reviews with senior leadership, and level up the rest of the engineering team on applied AI.

What We're Looking For?

Education


B.Tech / M.Tech in Computer Science or a related field, preferably from a reputed institute (IIT, BITS, NIT, or equivalent).

Experience


  • 10+ years of software engineering experience, with staff-level impact: technical influence and standard-setting that extends well beyond your own work. We weigh scope of impact over years alone.

  • A strong backend and distributed-systems foundation: the kind of depth that earns trust in any architecture review and lets you own the design of production services, not just consume them.

  • 2–3+ years hands-on building GenAI applications, having used LLMs extensively across a range of use cases (RAG, agents, structured extraction, content generation, etc.).

  • Strong conceptual grasp of Agentic flows and long-running agents: how they plan, use tools, manage memory/state, recover from errors, and incorporate human oversight. Hands-on experience is a plus; deep understanding is required even if you haven't shipped one in production.

  • Demonstrated judgment on model selection and quality-vs-cost-vs-latency trade-offs across RAG, prompting, agents, and fine-tuning: with a clear point of view on when each fits and when it doesn't.

  • Production experience with eval, observability, guardrails, and cost control for LLM systems.

  • Current, active awareness of AI research and model releases, able to separate durable shifts from hype and explain why they matter for us.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder skills, able to translate complex AI concepts for non-technical audiences and influence direction across the org.

Nice to Have


  • Hands-on experience building or operating autonomous / long-running agents.

  • LLM fine-tuning experience (LoRA/PEFT,RLHF/DPO). A plus, not a requirement.

  • Background in B2B SaaS or enterprise deployments.

  • Experience as the AI point person on a team or org, setting standards and levelling others up.


Benefits

Why Join Us?


  • Own the AI direction at a fast-growing startup: real, enterprise-grade GenAI systems customers run in production, not demos.

  • Direct line to the founding team and a seat in the decisions that shape the product and the org.

  • Work alongside a world-class team: engineers and operators from Amazon, McKinsey,IIT, and Stanford.

  • A fast growth curve, strong ownership, and competitive compensation with equity.

title: Vice President - Lead Site Reliability Engineer
description:
Shape the future of enterprise resilience at one of the world's most influential financial institutions.

As a Lead Site Reliability Engineer at JPMorganChase within Infrastructure Platforms, you bring deep technical expertise and a leadership mindset to one of the firm's most critical reliability domains. You will drive the design, automation, and continuous improvement of scalable backup, recovery, and data-protection services that safeguard the firm's most sensitive assets. In this role, you will influence senior stakeholders, mentor engineers across the team, and translate complex regulatory and security requirements into engineered, production-ready solutions. Your work directly strengthens the firm's operational resilience and positions the team at the forefront of cloud-native infrastructure engineering.

Job responsibilities

  • Build and operate distributed systems, platform services, APIs, automation frameworks, and cloud-native applications that underpin enterprise-scale backup and recovery capabilities
  • Embed site reliability engineering principles through reliability metrics, observability, incident learning, operational readiness reviews, and continuous improvement cycles
  • Lead architecture and engineering for scalable backup, recovery, immutable-data protection, and recovery-assurance services across hybrid and cloud environments
  • Drive automation-first, API-led, and self-service capabilities that reduce operational toil and measurably improve customer and stakeholder outcomes
  • Build cloud-native solutions using AWS services, infrastructure as code, continuous integration and delivery pipelines, and modern software-engineering practices
  • Design preventive and detective security controls, policy guardrails, automated validation, and audit-ready evidence to meet regulatory and compliance requirements
  • Apply enterprise-authorized AI capabilities to accelerate infrastructure analysis and design documentation, validating outputs and handling operational data in accordance with sensitivity and security requirements
  • Deliver telemetry, reporting, and operational intelligence that provide real-time visibility into backup health, compliance posture, and recovery readiness
  • Mentor engineers, influence senior stakeholders, and coordinate cross-team delivery with clear ownership and explicit dependency management

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Formal training or certification on site reliability engineering concepts and 5+ years applied experience
  • Demonstrated experience building distributed systems, platform services, APIs, automation frameworks, and cloud-native applications
  • Expertise in site reliability engineering practices, monitoring, telemetry, incident management, and production operational readiness, including hands-on experience with observability and monitoring platforms such as Dynatrace and Grafana
  • Deep knowledge of one or more infrastructure engineering domains including networking, storage engineering, deployment practices, integration, automation, scaling, resilience, or performance assessments
  • Strong knowledge of enterprise data protection, backup and recovery, cyber resilience, immutable storage, retention policies, and recovery testing
  • Advanced AWS experience spanning backup services, identity and access management, security controls, observability, and infrastructure automation
  • Proficiency in Python and at least one additional language such as Java, Go, or C#
  • Demonstrated experience using enterprise-authorized AI capabilities to support infrastructure engineering workflows, with strong validation habits and awareness of data sensitivity
  • Ability to review and validate AI-assisted recommendations before implementation, escalating when uncertain and ensuring outcomes align to resiliency, security, and auditability expectations
  • Ability to lead complex, cross-organizational initiatives and translate security, control, and regulatory requirements into engineered solutions

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Experience with enterprise backup platforms such as Cohesity or Commvault, and cloud-native backup services such as AWS Backup
  • Familiarity with container orchestration platforms such as Kubernetes or OpenShift in a production environment
  • Exposure to database platforms and cyber-recovery solutions within a regulated financial-services environment
  • Experience with operational analytics and data-driven approaches to infrastructure health and compliance reporting

title: Technical Program Manager, Hardware NPI & Server Platforms
description:
Oracle's Hardware Division within Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager to lead Hardware New Product Introduction (NPI) programs for next-generation GPU and CPU server platforms. This role owns end-to-end program execution, from initial product requirements and engineering development through hardware qualification, manufacturing readiness, production ramp, and market launch.

You will lead integrated cross-functional product teams spanning electrical, mechanical, and thermal engineering, firmware, operating systems, quality assurance, manufacturing, supply management, and sourcing. Working closely with engineering and OCI service teams, you will drive the delivery of test hardware and initial production infrastructure required to support OCI data centers and regional deployments.

Combining strong hardware systems knowledge with technical program leadership, you will translate product requirements into executable plans, resolve complex engineering dependencies, and drive alignment across teams to meet schedule, quality, cost, and deployment commitments. Success in this role requires technical judgment, proactive risk management, and the ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct reporting authority.

Technical Program Leadership & Execution

  • Own integrated product plans covering scope, milestones, resources, build quantities, budgets, technical dependencies, risks, and launch criteria.
  • Partner with product management and OCI service and technical program management teams to align product roadmaps, customer requirements, security expectations, and regional deployment needs.
  • Maintain integrated schedules and dependency plans, establish deliverables and acceptance criteria with functional owners, identify gaps early, and drive corrective actions through closure.
  • Lead cross-functional product reviews, establishing clear ownership, decisions, action items, and delivery commitments.
  • Communicate technical trade-offs, forecast dates, cost exposure, quality readiness, and recovery plans to engineering teams and executive stakeholders.
  • Prepare leadership briefings, including SVP-level reviews when required, and escalate unresolved decisions with supporting analysis, options, and recommendations.

Cross-Functional Hardware Engineering & Integration

  • Coordinate electrical engineering activities, including platform and board design milestones, power and interface requirements, GPU and CPU integration, system bring-up, electrical validation, and engineering change dependencies.
  • Align mechanical engineering activities involving chassis and rack integration, assembly, packaging, manufacturing requirements, mechanical verification, and resolution of fit or deployment issues.
  • Integrate BIOS, Baseboard Management Controller (BMC), and device firmware milestones with hardware builds and validation, tracking compatibility, management functionality, security requirements, update readiness, and release dependencies.
  • Coordinate operating system enablement, drivers, software compatibility, installation, and deployment readiness with hardware and firmware plans, driving resolution of cross-stack defects with engineering owners.
  • Partner with quality assurance teams to coordinate requirements-based test coverage, qualification, reliability, regression testing, defect disposition, and release evidence.
  • Diagnose integration and delivery challenges across engineering disciplines, evaluating alternatives based on performance, reliability, manufacturability, supply availability, cost, and schedule.

Manufacturing, Supply Chain & Product Launch

  • Align prototype, qualification, pilot, and production builds with factory capacity, tooling, test equipment, work instructions, yield targets, and manufacturing ramp plans.
  • Partner with supply management teams to align material demand, bill of materials (BOM) availability, allocations, and supplier delivery commitments with engineering builds and launch quantities.
  • Drive material shortage mitigation and qualified alternative plans in collaboration with supply management and engineering owners.
  • Coordinate supplier selection milestones, sourcing readiness, quotation inputs, cost targets, commercial dependencies, and supplier commitments, routing purchasing and contract approvals through authorized owners.
  • Collaborate with silicon suppliers, Original Design Manufacturers (ODMs), Joint Design Manufacturers (JDMs), and external manufacturing partners to align product development and delivery commitments.
  • Lead readiness reviews from development through production release, partnering with Supply Chain to present qualification results, open issues, material and factory readiness, firmware and software release status, and deployment evidence.
  • Ensure functional owners document acceptance results, resolve or formally disposition launch-blocking issues, obtain required functional approvals, and document residual risks and accountable owners.
  • Coordinate launch hardware delivery to OCI data centers and support manufacturing handoff to sustaining operations.

Stakeholder Leadership, Risk Management & Continuous Improvement

  • Lead cross-functional execution without direct reporting authority, building relationships across engineering organizations, lines of business, and external partners.
  • Apply independent technical judgment to moderately complex assignments, influencing decisions and driving alignment across competing priorities.
  • Provide evidence-based recommendations to management, escalating decisions beyond delegated authority when appropriate.
  • Drive improvements in hardware readiness reviews, validation processes, build execution, and engineering change control.
  • Seek diverse perspectives, mentor junior engineers and program managers, and provide task oversight as appropriate.
  • Coordinate vendors, contractors, and temporary staff as required.
  • Deliver significant impact on team results while contributing to broader organizational objectives.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

  • 12+ years of relevant experience in hardware engineering, technical program management, product development, or related disciplines, assessed with applicable education and experience equivalencies under Oracle's Career Level Guide.
  • Within this background, 5+ years managing technical programs spanning multiple teams and organizations from conception through delivery. These experience periods are not additive.
  • Bachelor's or master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Hardware Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, with relevant education and experience assessed under Oracle's equivalency guidance.
  • Advanced knowledge of hardware development and New Product Introduction (NPI) systems and processes, with broad knowledge of GPU or CPU platforms as a specialist area.
  • Demonstrated experience leading hardware development, qualification, or production introduction and working with external manufacturers and supply chain partners.
  • Technical fluency across electrical, mechanical, thermal, firmware, operating systems, and quality assurance workstreams, including the ability to challenge assumptions and investigate system integration issues using test data, vendor tools, and engineering logs.
  • Experience with integrated program planning, critical-path and dependency management, build readiness, risk mitigation, cost and budget tracking, and controlled change management.
  • Demonstrated judgment, analytical problem-solving, negotiation, and influence across internal teams and supplier organizations, supported by clear written and verbal communication.
  • Ability to partner with product management on roadmap and launch commitments and ensure product readiness meets security, quality, and deployment requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience working with NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel GPU and CPU platforms.
  • Experience supporting manufacturing ramp and supply readiness.
  • Experience with hardware adaptation for international deployment.
  • Experience delivering servers, racks, or related infrastructure into data center environments.
  • MBA or additional advanced business education.
