title: Technical Lead DevOps & Security
description:
About US:-

We turn customer challenges into growth opportunities. Material is a global strategy partner to the world’s most recognizable brands and innovative companies. Our people around the globe thrive by helping organizations design and deliver rewarding customer experiences.
We use deep human insights, design innovation and data to create experiences powered by modern technology. Our approaches speed engagement and growth for the companies we work with and transform relationships between businesses and the people they serve.
Srijan, a Material company, is a renowned global digital engineering firm with a reputation for solving complex technology problems using their deep technology expertise and leveraging strategic partnerships with top-tier technology partners. Be a part of an Awesome Tribe

Must-have skills:-

Azure platform security (primary):-

  • Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD): app registrations, service principals, OAuth2 scopes, delegated vs application permissions, On-Behalf-Of (OBO) token flows, consent model, resource-scoped permissions (Exchange App RBAC, RSC-style scoping)
  • Azure API Management (APIM): authoring and staging policies, per-client policy keyed on client ID, correlation-ID handling, content-safety and token-limit policies
  • Azure networking: NSGs, firewall / egress rules, private endpoints / private connectivity, subnet segmentation
  • Azure observability: Azure Monitor diagnostic settings, Log Analytics, Microsoft Sentinel, OpenTelemetry, KQL for validation and evidence queries

Engineering and DevOps:-

  • Reading and reasoning about application source code to derive least-privilege scope (which MCP servers, tools, and Graph resources an agent actually calls, read vs write, target resources). This is the load-bearing skill for DC-IAM-1
  • Building a shared instrumentation library / SDK (structured event emission, schema conformance, mandatory-by-design)
  • CI/CD and staged promotion through environments (DEV to UAT), infrastructure-as-config discipline
  • Comfort with a native-first, GA-only stance: prefer existing generally-available Azure controls over custom code; no preview-tier dependencies

Security engineering practice:

  • Default-deny and least-privilege as defaults
  • Fail-closed design (a control failure must never become a bypass)
  • Proving enforcement with a negative test (the disallowed path is shown to be blocked, not just the allowed path working)
  • Producing audit-grade evidence: before/after permission exports, allow/deny matrices, tamper/bypass tests, control-design and procedure writeups

Nice to Have:-

  • PlainID or another externalized policy decision point (PDP) / policy-based access control
  • AI agent platforms, LLM gateways, MCP (Model Context Protocol) hubs and connectors
  • LangSmith or similar LLM tracing tools Postgres (the MCP hub registration / scope model runs on it)
  • Prior work in a regulated / financial-services environment and familiarity with control-audit expectations (design gates, ARB / TRC / SOC sign-off)
  • Guardrail and content-safety tooling (Azure Content Safety, Prompt Shields, Groundedness)

Working conditions and expectations

  • Ground rules: native-first and GA-only; default-deny; fail closed for high-risk; one correlation ID end to end; confirm before changing shared platform config (APIM, network, identity changes affect every agent, so stage in DEV/UAT and validate before handoff)
  • Release model: build and stage each control through DEV then UAT, complete positive and negative validation and sign-off at UAT, then hand off to the client, who promotes to PROD through their own change management
  • Cadence: two-week sprints; MVP (audit-defensible, may be manual or lean on an existing process) for 7 of 8 controls by 9/25, then hardening to fully operational with evidence by mid-November
  • Collaboration: coordinate with client platform (Calvin's team), Cloud (network segmentation), and SecOps (dashboards, log-schema ingestion); design gates reviewed by ARB / TRC / SOC before UAT-to-client handoff
  • The real floor on speed is the DEV-to-UAT promotion cadence and per-control validation, not coding time. We build with AI coding agents assisting, so mechanical authoring compresses; the validation and sign-off floor does not

What success looks like:-

  • 7 of 8 platform controls at a minimally defensible (audit-holds-up) state by 9/25, DC-OBS-9 shortly after
  • Each control shipped with the three-artifact trio: control design, documented procedures, and a test plan with evidence including the negative test
  • Full McKinsey-built set hardened to fully operational with evidence by mid-November

title: Maintenance Lead - Multifamily Lease-Up & Stabilization
description:
Maintenance Lead – Multifamily Lease-Up & Stabilization
Location: Santana Ridge Apartments | Chandler, ArizonaPosition: Full-TimeCompensation: Competitive Pay, Based on ExperienceBenefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Short-Term Disability, Paid Time Off & Paid Holidays
Join CAM Properties – Help Lead Santana Ridge to Success!

CAM Properties is seeking an experienced, hands-on, and motivated Maintenance Lead to oversee maintenance operations at Santana Ridge Apartments in Chandler, Arizona.
This is an exciting opportunity for a skilled maintenance professional who takes pride in their work, enjoys leading a team, and understands the important role maintenance plays in a community's leasing success, resident satisfaction, and overall property performance.

As Santana Ridge continues through its lease-up and stabilization efforts, the Maintenance Lead will play a key role in ensuring apartments are move-in ready, service requests are completed efficiently, preventative maintenance is prioritized, and the community consistently delivers an exceptional living experience.

We are looking for more than someone who can complete repairs. We want a proactive leader who takes ownership of property conditions, motivates their team, maintains high standards, and works closely with the Community Manager to achieve occupancy and operational goals.

Key Responsibilities
Maintenance Operations & Team Leadership

Lead, train, and support onsite maintenance team members while promoting accountability, teamwork, and high-quality workmanship.
Assign, prioritize, and complete maintenance work orders while ensuring timely response and resolution.
Establish daily maintenance priorities and monitor productivity, work quality, and completion timelines.
Maintain strong communication with the Community Manager and leasing team regarding maintenance needs, apartment availability, and resident concerns.
Promote a positive, solutions-oriented work environment focused on efficiency, professionalism, and exceptional customer service.

Lease-Up, Apartment Turns & Stabilization

Play an active role in achieving the community's occupancy and stabilization goals by ensuring apartments are ready for leasing and move-in.
Coordinate and oversee apartment turns, make-ready schedules, inspections, and quality control.
Minimize apartment downtime and ensure vacant units are completed on schedule and meet CAM's presentation standards.
Partner with the leasing team to prioritize upcoming move-ins, model apartments, and units needed to support leasing activity.
Conduct final inspections to ensure apartments are clean, functional, and fully prepared for new residents.
Proactively identify maintenance issues that could delay leasing, move-ins, or resident satisfaction.

Preventative Maintenance & Property Standards

Develop and maintain preventative maintenance schedules for HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical equipment, appliances, and community amenities.
Perform and oversee routine repairs, troubleshooting, and preventative maintenance.
Conduct regular inspections of buildings, grounds, amenities, mechanical systems, and common areas.
Maintain excellent curb appeal, cleanliness, landscaping coordination, and overall community presentation.
Identify potential maintenance concerns early to reduce emergency repairs, unnecessary expenses, and resident disruption.
Ensure maintenance shops, equipment, tools, and inventory are organized, properly maintained, and safely stored.

Capital Improvements, Renovations & Vendor Coordination

Assist the Community Manager and regional leadership with coordinating interior improvements, exterior renovations, and capital improvement projects.
Monitor vendor and contractor work to ensure quality, timely completion, and minimal disruption to residents.
Assist with project inspections, scheduling, progress updates, and quality control.
Identify opportunities to improve property conditions, enhance curb appeal, and support long-term asset preservation.
Help manage maintenance expenses, supplies, and vendor costs while maintaining quality standards.

Resident Experience & Safety

Deliver exceptional customer service through timely repairs, professional communication, and respectful interactions with residents.
Respond promptly to resident maintenance concerns and ensure proper follow-up.

title: PRODUCT MANAGER K2
description:
Summary:

K2 is KOA's campground proprietary property management system. The Product Manager works with Engineering, Design, and other subject-matter experts to identify customer problems, prioritize opportunities, define desired outcomes, and deliver valuable product improvements.
The Product Manager owns assigned PM S domain product priorities and works with the cross-functional Product Team to develop solutions, refine requirements, and prepare work for delivery. This is a high-leverage individual-contributor role. The PM leads through evidence, facilitation, and influence, contributing to a trusted product roadmap that serves as the ultimate source of truth for executives, franchisees, and engineers.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Manage and continuously evolve the K2 product strategy and outcome-based roadmap across K2's product domains and delivery teams.
Lead continuous discovery with campground operators, front-desk staff, franchise stakeholders, and campers as part of the K2 quartet; run a recurring operator research cadence and synthesize findings into validated problems and prioritized opportunities.
Frame problems, not solutions: own the problem, customer, desired outcome, why-now, success metric, and priority for every investment, let the team discover the solution and the team decompose and own the stories.
Understand and comprehend the competitive and market intelligence for the campground management software category; help maintain the K2 competitive capability tracker and translate parity gaps into roadmap decisions.
Own product requirements at the product level, opportunity statements, objectives, personas, use cases and prioritize at the outcome level: define the target outcome, key results, and success measures for each roadmap investment before work enters delivery.
Operate the product intake model: convert stakeholder requests and operator escalations into evidence, assess them as opportunities, and protect delivery teams from unprioritized, unscored work entering the backlog directly. A request is evidence, not a requirement.
Partner with the product team on Ready-queue priorities, owning the “why,” the “what problem,” and priority between product opportunities and outcomes
Contribute to and lead at times the weekly Product Discovery cadence and the monthly K2 Product Review; communicate roadmap, outcomes, and learning to executive and franchise audiences. Maintain the roadmap and discovery record in the product management tool, distinct from delivery tracking in Jira.
Define adoption and measurement plans for every significant release; run Outcome Reviews so “done” is distinguished from “successful.”
Support the K2 commercialization thesis with market sizing, segmentation, and packaging analysis.
Champion and model the organization's transition from request-driven delivery to discovery-driven product management, including supporting the professional development of teammates growing toward product management.
Attendance at the team's core flow and product cadences, including daily flow stand-ups, replenishment, refinement, and review sessions is required.
In-person attendance will be required on a yearly cycle to attend departmental meetings and/or staff development meetings.

Non-Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

This job description is not intended to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

Required Education and Experience:

Bachelor's degree in a relevant field or equivalent professional experience.4 + years of software product experience.
A demonstrated continuous discovery practice, including recurring customer research, structured opportunity assessment, and evidence-based prioritization.
Proven experience building and communicating outcome-based roadmaps and defining product KPIs; strong analytical skills, with SQL or BI tool fluency a plus.
Experience partnering with delivery-facing product roles in an agile or flow-based delivery model.
Able to work as part of a cross-functional discovery group (PM, Design, Engineering, Business Stakeholders) where the team — not any single role — owns solutions and stories.
Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills; the ability to influence without authority across product, engineering, and franchise audiences.

Preferred Education and Experience:

Experience in hospitality technology, property management systems, reservation/booking platforms, marketplaces, or franchise business models preferred.
Software product management experience on B2B or B2C SaaS or platform products; candidates with strong adjacent experience (e.g., senior product ownership or business analysis with demonstrated discovery and outcome accountability) will be considered.

Physical Demands and Working Conditions:

Work is performed in an office environment and requires the ability to operate standard office equipment and keyboard, including lifting and carrying a laptop and other small items up to 20 pounds.
Prolonged exposure to computer screens and artificial lighting.
Use of repetitive motion, standing, bending, sitting, lifting, and walking short distances.
May be expected to drive a vehicle to KOA locations, other locations as directed, and conferences which requires close and distance vision, sitting, seeing and reading signs, traffic signals, other vehicles, etc. Travel occurs in all weather conditions, including extreme heat and cold.
Frequent in person interaction with KOA employees in various settings, where noise level is typically low to moderate, including office spaces.
Will experience occasional interruptions and shifting priorities.

title: Værkmester
description:
Vil du gøre en reel forskel for mennesker og samtidig have en alsidig hverdag?

Så er du måske vores nye værkmester i Nordvestsjællands Fængsler.

På værkstedet med de indsatte, der er placeret i lukket regi i Jyderup bliver du en vigtig del af hverdagen for de indsatte. Du får en arbejdsdag, hvor relationer, ansvar, sikkerhed og praktiske opgaver går hånd i hånd.

Du skal være med til at skabe struktur og meningsfuld beskæftigelse for de indsatte og samtidig bidrage til den daglige drift af fængslet. Det kræver både menneskelig forståelse, tydelig kommunikation og evnen til at bevare overblikket – også når dagene ikke går helt som planlagt.

Om jobbet

Som værkmester i Jyderup bliver du en del af fængslets beskæftigelse af de indsatte. De indsatte arbejder blandt andet med forskellige montageopgaver, kreative opgave og du vil være med til at vejlede og føre opsyn med arbejdet.

Du vil også sammen med de indsatte udføre mindre rengørings, reparations- og vedligeholdelsesopgaver.

En vigtig del af jobbet er at være med til at skabe en god balance mellem beskæftigelse, relationer og sikkerhed. Du får derfor en alsidig hverdag, hvor du både arbejder selvstændigt og samarbejder tæt med kolleger på tværs af værksteder og faggrupper. På det lukkede værksted er I som udgangspunkt altid to på arbejde, så det er vigtigt at du kan finde ind i et godt samarbejde med din kommende kollega.

Dine primære arbejdsopgaver

  • Føre opsyn med og vejlede de indsatte i deres arbejdsopgaver.
  • Udlevere og registrere cellearbejde til de indsatte i arresten.
  • Deltage i fængslets daglige drift og efter behov afløse på andre værksteder.
  • Samarbejde med andre værksteder og faggrupper.
  • Deltage i sagsbehandlingen omkring de indsatte, herunder registrering i PUMA m.m.
  • Bidrage til den dynamiske sikkerhed i fængslet.
  • Registrere arbejdsdusør i Danmarks Fængslers økonomisystem.
  • Udføre mindre reparations- og vedligeholdelsesopgaver sammen med de indsatte.
Hvem er du?

Vi leder efter dig, der kan se mennesket bag den indsatte, og som samtidig kan være tydelig og sætte de nødvendige grænser.

Vi lægger især vægt på, at du:

  • Er en god menneskekender og møder det enkelte menneske med empati og respekt.
  • Har en naturlig og personlig autoritet og kan skabe ro, struktur og orden.
  • Kommunikerer klart og tydeligt om regler, rammer og forventninger.
  • Kan håndtere mennesker, der befinder sig i krise eller svære situationer.
  • Har gode samarbejdsevner og bidrager positivt til fællesskabet.
  • Er fleksibel, omstillingsparat og samtidig i stand til at arbejde selvstændigt.
  • Trives i en omskiftelig hverdag, hvor ikke to dage nødvendigvis er ens.
  • Kan fungere i en tværfaglig medarbejdergruppe med mange forskellige opgaver og løbende nye tiltag.
  • Er indstillet på at gennemføre Kriminalforsorgens interne værkmesteruddannelse, hvis du ikke allerede er uddannet værkmester.
Som værkmester får du mulighed for at gøre en konkret forskel i hverdagen. Du bliver en del af et fagligt fællesskab, hvor vi sammen arbejder for at skabe en tryg og struktureret hverdag for både indsatte og medarbejdere.

Hvis du motiveres af at arbejde med mennesker, tage ansvar og have en hverdag, hvor du aldrig helt ved, hvad dagen bringer, så glæder vi os til at høre fra dig.

Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår
Stillingen er på 37 timer ugentligt.

Ansættelse sker i henhold til Tjenestemandsloven og lønindplacering sker i henhold til lønaftalen mellem Kriminalforsorgen og Fængselsforbundet i Danmark, provinssats. Stillingen er indplaceret i løngruppe 2 eller med rette erhvervsfaglig uddannelse i løngruppe 3.

Det er en forudsætning for ansættelse, at du i forbindelse med samtalen giver dit samtykke til, at Danmarks Fængsler må indhente og vurdere oplysninger om dig i det Centrale Kriminalregister.

Ansættelsesområde er Justitsministeriet med tilhørende institutioner.
Arbejdsstedet er Jyderup Fængsel, Søbæksparken 136, 4450 Jyderup

Ansøgning
Du søger stillingen via knappen ”søg stillingen”. Ansøgning, CV og dokumentation for uddannelse samt andet relevant materiale skal være modtaget i rekrutteringssystemet senest fredag den 30. oktober 2026.

Som tjenestemand skal du tillige inden ansøgningsfristen den fredag den 30.oktober 2026 uploade din ansøgning, samt anmode din nærmeste chef om at få en udtalelse/bedømmelse. Bedømmelsen skal uploades senest den 5. november 2026.

Vi indkalder til samtaler løbende.

Hvis du indkaldes til samtale, skal du til samtalen medbringe billedidentifikation, f.eks. pas eller kørekort.

Inden ansættelse skal vi modtage dokumentation for CV.

Alle interesserede uanset personlig baggrund opfordres til at søge.

Yderligere oplysninger
Nærmere oplysninger fås ved henvendelse til enhedschef Kenni Lyngberg tlf. 72 55 23 33.

Om Danmarks Fængsler, Fængselskreds Øst
Fængselskreds Øst består af et kredskontor, åbne og lukkede fængsler, arresthuse og tilsyn, samt fodlænkeafdelinger, transport og bevogtning, udrejsecenter og udlændingecenter fordelt på hele Sjælland, Bornholm og Færøerne.

I alt ca. 2300 ansatte.

title: Production Technician 1
description:
The North America team is seeking a Production Technician for our Paris, IL facility.
The Production Technician is responsible for operating and maintaining machines, such as Sheet Cutting Lasers, BLM Tube Lasers, Plasma Cutting Lasers and Lathe/Milling CNC precision machines. The technician must follow detailed instructions to ensure the accuracy of each product. They must inspect parts for any defects or inconsistencies and adjust as needed. The technician must also monitor the machines to ensure they are running smoothly and efficiently. They must have a good understanding of the equipment and be able to troubleshoot any issues that arise. The technician must be able to read and understand technical documents, follow safety guidelines, and maintain accurate records of production. This position is also required to run equipment in other areas as needed.

Your Impact

Set-up, adjust, program, calibrate and perform preventative maintenance on specific precision machines.
Machine material to specification from job orders at a level of output that minimizes production delays.
Monitor machine performance and ensure consistent quality throughout production cycles.
Utilize quality checks; inspect finished parts using precision measuring tools to specification and quality standards.
Document and communicate quality findings according to company standards.
Troubleshoot and resolve operational issues by adjusting machine offsets, speeds, and feeds as required to maintain production efficiency and quality.
Conduct routine machine upkeep, including cleaning, and lubrication.
Maintain a clean and orderly work area to 5S Standards.
Follow all aspects of Grain & Protein Technologies/GSI Paris Lean and Quality Management systems.
Other responsibilities as assigned.

Your Experience and Qualifications

High school diploma or GED.
2 + years of manual and CNC machine operation experience in manufacturing setting preferred.
Ability to read, write and use basic math skills (addition, subtraction, multiplication and division).
Proficiency in manual and CNC machine programming.
Proficiency in reading blueprints/technical drawings and use of precision measuring instruments.
Strong mechanical aptitude with the ability to follow precise instructions.
Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
Ability to operate overhead crane and sit down forklift.
Ability to lift 50 pounds on a continuous bases.
Ability to communicate effectively with peers, managers and across departments.

Your Compensation and Benefits
Expected hourly rate for this role will be $23.81 - $27.98, plus gain share eligibility. This is dependent upon job related knowledge, experience, and skills.

Benefits will include the ability to elect health care and wellness plans, dental and vision plans, flexible and virtual work options (where available), 401(k) Savings Plan with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, health savings and flexible spending accounts, reimbursement for continuing education, life insurance, and other supplemental insurance plans.

Your Workplace and Travel
You will be working onsite based in Paris, IL.

title: Wiring Technician
description:
About Piab Group

At Piab Group, we improve our customers' productivity, sustainability, and safety through evolving industrial automation and have done so since 1951. We believe in an automated world where no resources are wasted, and no humans are injured. With annual sales of ~3 billion SEK and more than 1400 employees, Piab is a global organization, serving customers in more than 100 countries from a vast network of subsidiaries and channel partners. Since 2018, Piab Group has been owned by Patricia Industries, part of Investor AB.

In 2024, Piab Group acquired Alum-a-Lift, further enhancing its capabilities in ergonomic material handling solutions. Alum-a-Lift designs and manufactures turnkey ergonomic lifting solutions for companies around the world. From single custom units to multiple devices to entire lifting systems, our proven solutions help manufacturers meet their material handling needs safely and efficiently.

You can expect the following with us:

Innovative Culture: Be part of a team that thrives on creativity and innovation.
Global Impact: Work with a company that is a world leader in vacuum transport solutions.
Global Presence: Piab has 25+ sales offices and over 900 partners worldwide, ensuring a vast network and global reach
Sustainable Vision: Contribute to an automated world, promoting safety and efficiency.
Professional Growth: Access opportunities for continuous learning and career advancement.
Collaboration: Join a workplace that values collaboration and a wide range of perspectives.
Stable employer: As part of Patricia Industries and connected to the Wallenberg family, Piab benefits from strong support and a commitment to long-term growth and sustainability.

Job Mission

The wiring Technician ensures timely and accurate wiring of lifts and lift components per Alum-a-Lift’s specifications and procedures.

Key Responsibilities

  • Clean lifts and parts to prepare them for shipment per provided schedule to meet or exceed customer’s expectations.
  • Assemble electrical components and modules according to CAD drawings and photos.
  • Soldering and de-soldering.
  • Trains to be able to utilize various tools and equipment to clean and prepare lifts and parts for packing, as well as packing of the lifts and parts.

  • Work in the department as a team member to produce products per manufacturing specifications to achieve or exceed the production, quality standards and goals.
  • Move and handle materials as necessary.
  • Perform routine cleaning to include sweeping and mopping floors, wiping down equipment, and participating in rotating schedule for cleaning bathrooms and break area.
  • Keep work area neat and orderly.
  • Perform any other assignment requested by lead, supervisor or production manager.

In this role you are required to act accordingly to the Piab Code of Conduct and know and follow the Piab values, mission and routines.

Skills and Abilities

  • Strong attention to detail and manual dexterity for precise assembly and soldering work.
  • Ability to read and interpret CAD drawings, schematics, and wiring diagrams.
  • Solid understanding of basic electrical principles and color coding of wires.
  • Ability to use hand tools, soldering irons, crimpers, and electrical testing equipment safely and effectively.
  • Good problem-solving and troubleshooting skills for wiring and component issues.
  • Strong time management skills and ability to maintain accuracy in a fast-paced environment.
  • Team-oriented attitude with effective communication skills.
  • Commitment to quality, safety, and continuous improvement.

Experience and Education

  • High school diploma or GED required; technical or vocational training in electrical technology or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in electrical wiring, assembly, or related manufacturing environment.

Key Interfaces

  • This position reports to the Wiring Lead

  • Interacts with Assembly Shop Supervisor
  • Interacts closely with Production Manager
  • This role currently has no direct reports

Travel
  • No regular travel

Job Type

FLSA Status
  • Hourly

title: Architect  (ServiceNow IRM)- Texas
description:
Category: Technology

Location:


The ServiceNowIRM Architect leads the design and delivery of scalable ServiceNow IntegratedRisk Management solutions for enterprise clients. The Architect translatescomplex business, risk, regulatory, and technical requirements into solutionarchitectures, implementation strategies, workflows, integrations, reporting,and automation aligned with Templar Shield standards and ServiceNow leadingpractices.

The Architectworks directly with stakeholders across risk, compliance, internal audit,cybersecurity, privacy, legal, technology, finance, and operations. This roleprovides architectural direction throughout discovery, design, configuration,testing, deployment, stabilization, and adoption while helping clientsestablish and mature sustainable governance, risk, compliance, audit, andresilience programs.

This is asenior, technical, client-facing consulting role that provides designauthority, leads Engineers, and works with Managers to ensure successfuldelivery. The Architect also helps clients evaluate and implement AI-enabledIRM capabilities using ServiceNow Otto, AI Control Tower, intelligentautomation, and agentic workflows. These capabilities must be designed withappropriate security, privacy, governance, explainability, human oversight, andresponsible-use controls.


Requirements

Primary Responsibilities:

ClientConsulting and Solution Leadership

  • Lead discovery sessions, stakeholder interviews, requirements workshops, maturity assessments, design sessions, and solution reviews with business, technical, and executive stakeholders.
  • Develop a clear understanding of each client’s business objectives, risk and compliance obligations, governance structure, operating model, technology environment, program maturity, and desired outcomes.
  • Translate complex business, risk, regulatory, operational, and technical requirements into scalable solution architectures, implementation strategies, roadmaps, and future-state operating models.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor by explaining architectural options, technical dependencies, implementation risks, design tradeoffs, and recommended approaches to client stakeholders.
  • Maintain alignment among client stakeholders, Managers, Engineers, product teams, and third-party vendors throughout solution design and delivery.

ServiceNow IRM Architecture andDelivery

  • Lead the architecture, design, and delivery of ServiceNow IRM solutions across Risk Management, Policy and Compliance Management, Audit Management, Third-Party Risk Management, Business Continuity Management, Operational Resilience, Regulatory Change Management, Issues Management, and related capabilities.
  • Define solution architecture across IRM applications, including data models, security, risk taxonomies, control structures, assessment methodologies, issues, indicators, approvals, workflows, integrations, and reporting.
  • Determine the appropriate use of out-of-the-box functionality, configuration, integration, automation, or custom development based on client requirements and ServiceNow leading practices.
  • Provide architectural oversight and targeted hands-on support across ServiceNow IRM applications while guiding Engineers responsible for configuration, development, testing, and deployment activities.
  • Advise clients on governance, risk management, regulatory compliance, internal controls, policy management, audit, third-party risk, business continuity, operational resilience, and sustainable IRM program management.

Integration, Data, Reporting, andAutomation

  • Design integrations between ServiceNow IRM and enterprise platforms, data repositories, regulatory-content providers, risk and compliance tools, security technologies, financial systems, and other business applications.
  • Define integration patterns, APIs, data mappings, transformation rules, reconciliation logic, synchronization schedules, error handling, monitoring, and support requirements.
  • Develop data architecture and governance strategies that support accurate risk, control, policy, audit, issue, assessment, indicator, entity, and regulatory information across IRM applications.
  • Define reporting and analytics strategies, including key performance indicators, key risk indicators, dashboards, data sources, audience-specific views, Performance Analytics, and executive reporting.
  • Evaluate ServiceNow Otto, AI Control Tower, automation, and agentic workflow capabilities for IRM use cases while ensuring appropriate security, privacy, governance, explainability, human oversight, and responsible use.

TechnicalLeadership and Quality Assurance

  • Develop and maintain solution architecture documents, integration designs, data models, process flows, functional specifications, architectural decisions, implementation guidance, and supporting technical documentation.
  • Establish technical standards and review configurations, workflows, integrations, data models, automation, and reporting for security, scalability, performance, maintainability, and upgrade compatibility.
  • Provide technical direction to Engineers and consultants, assign design and configuration activities, resolve complex technical issues, and validate completed work.
  • Define solution acceptance criteria and oversee system, integration, regression, and user acceptance testing, deployment readiness, production transition, and post-deployment stabilization.
  • Identify architectural risks, technical debt, assumptions, dependencies, and complex design issues and work with Managers and client stakeholders to develop mitigation plans and guide clients away from unnecessary customization.

Practice and Sales Support:

TheServiceNow IRM Architect supports Templar Shield’s business development andpractice growth by providing solution leadership and subject-matter expertisethroughout the sales process.

  • Support Practice Leads in identifying, qualifying, shaping, and expanding ServiceNow IRM opportunities within new and existing client accounts.
  • Participate in pre-sales discovery sessions, solution demonstrations, technical workshops, capability presentations, and executive discussions.
  • Lead solution scoping and contribute to architecture approaches, staffing models, delivery plans, effort estimates, pricing inputs, proposals, Statements of Work (SOWs), and responses to Requests for Proposals (RFPs).
  • Develop solution approaches that clearly define scope, assumptions, dependencies, integration requirements, risks, staffing needs, and delivery estimates.
  • Help develop reusable service offerings, implementation methodologies, reference architectures, integration patterns, demonstrations, accelerators, templates, and training materials.

Technical Knowledge and Skills:

Candidates must demonstratestrong solution architecture, platform, and IRM knowledge, including:

  • Strong knowledge of ServiceNow IRM applications, data models, workflows, workspaces, and related platform capabilities.
  • Experience designing solutions across Risk Management, Policy and Compliance Management, Audit Management, Third-Party Risk Management, Business Continuity Management, Operational Resilience, Regulatory Change Management, Issues Management, or related applications.
  • Strong working knowledge of ServiceNow platform architecture, application scope, data models, security, access controls, reporting, dashboards, and platform governance.
  • Ability to evaluate requirements and determine the appropriate use of out-of-the-box functionality, configuration, integration, automation, or custom development.
  • Experience designing IRM workflows, assessments, risk and control processes, policies, audits, issues, indicators, approvals, taxonomies, attestations, and related automation.
  • Experience defining enterprise integration strategies using REST and SOAP web services, APIs, Integration Hub, MID Server, import sets, transform maps, and established ServiceNow integration patterns.
  • Ability to develop reporting and analytics strategies, including key performance indicators, key risk indicators, dashboards, executive reporting, Performance Analytics, and supporting data sources.
  • Experience reviewing solution designs, configurations, integrations, automation, and data models for security, scalability, performance, maintainability, and upgrade compatibility.
  • Familiarity with data migration, Automated Test Framework, source control, application deployment, update management, release management, and ServiceNow upgrade practices.
  • Working knowledge of JavaScript, Flow Designer, Integration Hub, business rules, and other ServiceNow scripting and automation capabilities.
  • Familiarity with ServiceNow Otto, AI Control Tower, and AI-enabled or agentic workflow capabilities, including the governance, security, privacy, explainability, human oversight, and responsible-use considerations associated with their implementation.

Qualifications

  • Five or more years of ServiceNow platform experience, including experience in a Solution Architect, Technical Lead, or comparable architecture role, with at least three years focused on ServiceNow Integrated Risk Management.
  • Experience leading enterprise ServiceNow implementations through discovery, design, configuration, testing, deployment, stabilization, and adoption.
  • Experience leading stakeholder interviews, requirements workshops, design sessions, solution reviews, and executive-level presentations.
  • Strong understanding of governance, risk management, compliance, internal controls, policy management, audit, assessments, third-party risk, and related business processes.
  • Experience coordinating multiple technical and functional workstreams and managing competing priorities and deliverables in a consulting environment.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, including the ability to evaluate technical tradeoffs and resolve complex architectural issues.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain technical and functional concepts to business stakeholders, technical teams, and executive leadership.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate with geographically dispersed teams, mentor consultants and engineers, and provide solution guidance without direct people-management responsibilities.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Business, Risk Management, Finance, Accounting, or a related discipline preferred.
  • ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA) certification required
  • Willingness to travel up to 50 percent based on client and project requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist – Risk and Compliance, Certified Application Developer, or other relevant ServiceNow certifications.
  • Experience implementing multiple ServiceNow IRM applications, including advanced, enterprise, or cross-application solutions.
  • Experience conducting IRM maturity assessments, developing multiyear roadmaps, and designing governance programs, target operating models, or enterprise risk-transformation initiatives.
  • Familiarity with regulatory and control frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 2, COSO, COBIT, PCI DSS, HIPAA, CIS Controls, and FFIEC.
  • Experience supporting regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, technology, energy, utilities, telecommunications, or the public sector.
  • Experience with related ServiceNow capabilities such as Security Operations, IT Service Management, IT Operations Management, CMDB, Privacy Management, AI Control Tower, or third-party governance, risk, and compliance platforms.
  • Experience developing data-migration, integration, reporting, dashboard, analytics, or platform-governance strategies within enterprise ServiceNow environments.
  • Experience developing consulting methodologies, reusable service offerings, delivery accelerators, reference architectures, intellectual property, thought leadership, or go-to-market materials.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation + annual performance-based bonus
  • 100% remote-first culture
  • Benefits include health, dental, LTD, and life insurance coverage
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Reimbursement for job-related training and certifications
  • Work on frontier projects at the cutting edge of AI + Risk Management

title: Website Contact Page Review Assistant
description:
Website Contact Page Review Assistant

Office Administration · Website Content · Remote · Full-time or part-time
Hourly range £26.00–£28.00

People use a website’s contact page when they need a way forward.

If an address, form link or opening detail is out of date, the customer may never reach the right team. The Website Contact Page Review Assistant checks assigned pages against information the organisation has approved for publication. The position is remote and online, combining simple website review with careful office administration. You would identify discrepancies and make limited updates where authorised, not redesign the site or decide what information the business should publish.

The starting point for each review is an approved source. That might be a current contact list, an instruction from the responsible team or a documented change request. You would open the published page, compare the relevant details and note what differs. A page could contain several contact routes: an email link, an online form and a department phone number. Your job is to check the route specified in the assignment and avoid changing a different team’s details just because they look unusual.

What the review produces

For a straightforward correction, the work product may be an updated page with a note of what changed and a check that the live version shows the approved detail. In another case, you may prepare a clear issue report for the person who can make the edit. If the source material itself conflicts, you should ask which information is current before making the page look more certain than the team actually is. A broken link should be described with the page it appears on and the destination it was meant to reach.

A useful report identifies:

  • The page address or name and the particular contact element affected.
  • What the published page currently says or does.
  • The approved source that shows the expected information.
  • Whether the page was corrected, submitted for approval or left pending clarification.

The report should let the next colleague act without having to retrace the entire review.

This role does not require coding. The employer will teach its content system and how to preview or submit an authorised change. You should understand that an edit saved in a content screen may not yet appear to visitors. After an approved update, you would check the displayed page or note that publication still needs a colleague’s action. Small visual details matter too: a link should have useful text, and a corrected number should not be left in a paragraph beside an old number.

The tasks could include:

  • Checking an assigned contact page against approved information.
  • Testing an email link or form route without submitting unnecessary personal details.
  • Noting a mismatch in a phone number, address or contact instruction.
  • Preparing a permitted correction in the online content system.
  • Previewing the change and checking that unrelated text remains intact.
  • Asking for confirmation when two sources disagree.
  • Recording which page was reviewed and the result.
  • Passing a technical form failure to the person who maintains that system.

Customer service experience can be helpful because you can imagine what a visitor needs from the page. It is not required, and you will not be running a customer help desk. Previous website administration or office administrative work is also useful but optional. Beginners are welcome if they can compare a webpage with a supplied source, write a specific note and learn a simple publishing process. No specialist SEO, design or developer skill is needed for this introductory role.

You may work through a list of pages or handle approved updates as they arrive. Some require a change; others can be confirmed as accurate. You should record both outcomes, so the team does not repeat the same check without knowing it was completed. The job suits someone who is willing to check the result rather than assume a saved edit has worked. A suitable home office setup supports careful review of online pages and written instructions.

Terms and application

The opening offers remote hours on a full-time or part-time basis. The rate is £26.00–£28.00 an hour. The company’s exact website tools and approval steps will be covered in training.

Please point to any experience checking information, maintaining a page or writing a concise correction note. If you have updated a club site, course page or shared document, that may be relevant even without a formal web job.

We welcome applicants who can learn the editor and work carefully with an approved source. If you’re selected for the next step, you may be asked to complete an application on the hiring company’s website. An initial CV is enough to show the types of tasks you have handled.

title: Senior AI Test Engineer
description:
This is a remote position.

Senior AI Test Engineer

Location: Remote

About the Role

Alternative Path is looking for a Senior AI Test Engineer to lead quality assurance on a client engagement with a leading financial data and analytics company that has built AI agent systems (chatbots, RAG-based research/report generation, MCP-based tool-calling agents) on top of its proprietary datasets for its own clients. This is a senior, client-facing role: you'll own the test strategy for these systems end-to-end, working directly with the client's engineering team to validate accuracy, reliability, and safety before these agents reach financial industry end-users — where hallucinations or bad data retrieval carry real business risk.

This is not conventional QA. You'll be building evaluation frameworks and datasets, running systematic evals, and defining quality bars for non-deterministic, LLM-driven systems operating over complex financial data.

What You'll Do
  • Own the test and evaluation strategy for the client's AI agent systems — chatbots, RAG-based research/report generation, and MCP-based tool-calling agents
  • Design and build eval suites covering accuracy, groundedness/faithfulness to source data, task completion, latency, and safety
  • Build and curate golden datasets reflecting real client use cases and financial-data edge cases (ambiguous queries, stale data, conflicting sources, numerical precision)
  • Use eval/observability tooling such as LangSmith (or equivalents — Ragas, DeepEval, Braintrust, Langfuse, PromptFoo) to trace, score, and monitor agent runs
  • Define and track RAG-specific metrics (retrieval precision/recall, hallucination rate, citation/source accuracy) — critical given the systems sit on top of financial datasets where correctness is non-negotiable
  • Evaluate MCP-based tool-calling behavior — correct tool selection, multi-step task execution, failure handling
  • Design regression testing so prompt, model, or data-pipeline changes don't silently degrade quality
  • Run structured red-teaming for hallucinations, prompt injection, and unsafe/incorrect financial outputs
  • Act as the primary quality point of contact with the client's engineering stakeholders — translating findings into clear, actionable risk assessments
  • Mentor/guide any junior QA resources staffed onto the engagement as it scales
  • Build automation to integrate evals into CI pipelines where feasible

What We're Looking For

Must-haves

  • 3+ years in software QA/testing, with hands-on senior-level experience evaluating LLM-based or agentic AI systems (not just traditional QA)
  • Direct experience with eval frameworks/tools — LangSmith strongly preferred; also acceptable: Ragas, DeepEval, PromptFoo, Braintrust, Langfuse
  • Strong understanding of RAG architecture and how to independently evaluate retrieval quality vs. generation quality
  • Practical familiarity with MCP (Model Context Protocol) or comparable agent tool-calling frameworks
  • Strong Python skills for building test harnesses, scoring pipelines, and automation
  • Experience designing evaluation approaches for non-deterministic systems (probabilistic scoring, not binary pass/fail)
  • Comfortable working directly with client engineering teams — strong communication, able to explain quality risk to both technical and business stakeholders
  • Prior experience in a client services / consulting QA environment (this is a client-facing engagement, not an internal product team)

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience testing AI systems in fintech, capital markets, or data/analytics domains
  • Familiarity with financial data accuracy/compliance considerations (numerical precision, source traceability, audit trails)
  • Exposure to LLM red-teaming/safety evaluation practices
  • Experience with browser-automation agent testing (Playwright or similar)

Why This Role Matters

The client's end-users rely on these agents for financial research and decision-making — the cost of a hallucinated number or a wrong source is high. You'll be the senior technical authority ensuring these systems are trustworthy before they ship, working at the intersection of AI evaluation and financial-data correctness.

title: Vice President, Venue Business
description:
Arium Networks builds and operates small cell networks that are shaping the future of wireless connectivity. As demand for faster, more reliable wireless coverage continues to grow, small cell technology is becoming essential to how communities stay connected. Our company brings together an established infrastructure, existing client base, and deep industry expertise, while offering the rare opportunity to step into an early‑stage environment where your ideas matter and your contributions shape what comes next - helping define how we work, what we build, and how we scale. Joining Arium Networks allows you to grow your career while building technology that will influence how people connect in the years ahead.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Vice President, Venue Business leads Arium's venue / distributed antenna system (DAS) business strategy and execution — which includes a portfolio of 150+ active, installed venues (major entertainment companies, premier sports venues, and college campuses) that generates material, critical annual cashflow for the company, together with the pursuit of new venue opportunities. This role holds full budget accountability for Arium's venue/DAS business, a distinct department and broad operating area encompassing real estate capital spend, account management and sales headcount, and P&L performance. and owns the health of the existing venue base and the growth of the venue pipeline and is accountable for building a team and operating model that is scalable and aligned directly with achievement of business goals and objectives. As a member of Arium’s commercial leadership team, the VP also partners with carrier sales leadership to design and negotiate MNO partnership programs that secure Arium exclusive rights to pursue long-term rights at targeted venues.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Design and implement team structure, develop recommendations and implement the right specialization and incentives, and ensure the business is positioned to defend its existing revenue base while pursuing new growth in close partnership with key stakeholders such as the carrier sales organization.
Own the performance, retention, and growth of Arium's 150+ existing venue relationships, ensuring account management practices protect the business against competitive churn at contract renewal.
Identify and pursue expansion opportunities within the existing venue base, including cross-sell into other properties held by the same customers or their principals, and adjacent offerings (rooftops, towers, edge computing, private cellular, converged building automation).
Lead pursuit and closing of new venue opportunities, securing real estate rights and carrying transactions through to anchor tenant / network build.
MNO Partnership Programs: Collaborate with carrier sales leadership to design, propose, and negotiate MNO partnership programs, for both venue-funded and carrier-funded venue programs, that result in Arium securing exclusive rights to pursue long-term rights at designated venues. Jointly define program structure, target venue lists, funding and economic terms, and the scope and duration of exclusivity with each carrier; lead Arium’s side of program negotiations; and convert program exclusivity into executed long-term venue agreements that meet Arium’s return hurdles.
Ensure the team secures venues and negotiates terms that allow Arium to meet its targeted and required return hurdles on invested capital; although the role holds no direct capital authority, its negotiated deal terms set the foundation for the return earned on each network investment.
Own team structure, hiring, and compensation design recommendations for the venue business strategically planning for the typical cycle time (2 – 3 years) from hire to revenue.
Build and lead a team of Directors of Real Estate, account managers, and sales representatives; move the team from a generalist, regionally organized model toward vertical specialization (e.g., hospitality, healthcare, gaming, sports, CRO).
Lead the Sales Engineer function, ensuring strong technical sales support for the IT/RF-facing, often highly technical sales to venue owners.
Partner with functional and cross-functional leadership to provide cohesive direction toward Arium goals. Work closely with the carrier (MNO) sales organization to ensure early and ongoing alignment on strategy and tactics, including the vetting of potential sales opportunities so that every pursued venue has carrier sponsorship and a realistic path to being sold to a carrier, avoiding investment in venues the carrier organization cannot ultimately sell. Coordinate with the Business Development Lead on carrier-sponsored program opportunities, including venues brought under MNO partnership programs, and hand off / receive venues appropriately.
Communicate effectively with customers, potential customers, and external parties such as vendors, regulatory bodies, and municipalities.
Prepare and present business status and results updates including pipeline, existing-account health, MNO partnership program status, and investment/return performance to the CCO, the CEO, and Board as required.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO SUCCEED
What Does Success Look Like

Existing venue base retained through renewal cycles with minimal to no loss to competitors or venue sele-performance.
Specialized teams, capable of defending existing accounts and pursuing new business.
Demonstrated new-business pipeline growth sourced from RFPs, market-level sales efforts, and carrier-sponsored programs, each pursued only with Arium sales carrier sponsorship.
MNO partnership programs (venue-funded and carrier-funded) executed with carrier partners, securing carrier exclusive rights to pursue designated venues, and converted into executed long-term venue agreements.
Measurable cross-sell / expansion revenue from the existing venue base.

Required Experience and Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
15+ years of related experience, including 5+ years in a senior leadership role, acquired through accomplishments of applicable knowledge, duties, scope, and skills reflective of the level. Proven leadership experience in venue, DAS, small cell, or related wireless/real estate infrastructure sales and account management.
Extensive senior leadership experience with proven ability to effectively lead large teams in the development and implementation of complex initiatives.
Track record of building and leading a sales and/or account management team, including specialization and delegation, not solely individual production.
Experience working with or alongside Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) and understanding of carrier sales processes and priorities.
Demonstrated success structuring and negotiating complex commercial partnerships or programs with MNOs or other tier 1 counterparties, including exclusivity, funding, and economic terms.
Experience operating successfully in an environment with long sales cycles (multi-year) and forward-looking staffing/pipeline planning.
Strong executive presence; ability to engage and influence senior decision-makers internally and externally including large venue owners (entertainment companies, sports venues, universities) and their broader real estate organizations.
Experience selling into or managing relationships with tier 1 real estate owners; ideally including sales or account management experience selling solutions such as building automation systems into the real estate vertical market.
Experience with, or ability to quickly learn, adjacent wireless infrastructure and services offerings (rooftops, towers, edge computing, private cellular, converged building automation) is a plus.

Where you will work
This role falls into our hybrid work model, which is 2-days work from home (Friday and Monday) and 3-days in the office (Tuesday through Thursday) to optimize collaboration, relationship building and key stakeholder engagement and may require some travel as needed.

Compensation
The pay range offered for this position is $220,000 - $303,000 annually. A candidate’s offer is determined by various factors including but not limited to, depth of experience, role-related knowledge and skills, relevant education or training, internal alignment, and work location. Depending on the position offered, the compensation package may also include incentive compensation opportunities in the form of a discretionary annual cash bonus or commissions, and equity incentives

YOUR COMPANY BENEFITS
At Arium Networks we do our best to ensure you have access to the resources you need to live a healthy and happy life no matter where you are in life. Our benefits are built around your individual needs, covering physical, mental, and financial health and designed to enhance your quality of life.

We are proud to offer a full suite of health and wealth benefits for you and your loved ones. Below are a few of the key highlights of the many benefits we provide.

Comprehensive healthcare plans with highly company subsidized premiums and up to $2,000 annual company contribution to your Health Savings Account (HSA base plan for employee and dependents).
Market-leading 401(k) plan, which includes up to 10% company contributions through our 5% match and 5% profit sharing program (based on employee contributions).
New-child leave up to 8 weeks of 100% paid leave upon birth or legal adoption of a new child. Birth mothers are eligible for up to 8 weeks of additional 100% paid medical leave.
Tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 per year of eligible tuition and fees.
Arium Networks scholarship program awarding up to $10,000 per recipient each year for eligible dependent children of employees and interns.
Matching charitable contributions to qualified charitable organizations of up to $1,000 per year per teammate.
Generous paid time-off for eligible full-time employees (minimum 18 days per year based on years of service).
10 company holidays plus 2 floating holiday.

Additional responsibilities will include performing sampling for chemical and physical hazards, writing reports and assisting with maintaining the Emergency Response program, drills, and personnel training. The selected candidate will also serve in a reserve role for emergency response, during and after regular work hours.

Employment planned to begin in December.

Required Qualifications:

  • Must be a student currently enrolled in Utah State University’s Industrial Hygiene program
  • Must be able to commit to 40 hours per week during the summer and remain working for 20 hours per week during the school year between the hours of 8:00am-5:00pm on weekdays
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Must be willing to build positive relationships throughout the organization to enhance the safety and health culture
  • Must be observant and willing to correct unsafe behavior
  • Strong computer skills and a good working knowledge of Microsoft Office
  • Must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., or other U.S. person
Preferred Qualifications:
  • HAZWOPER certification is a plus
  • Prefer someone earlier in the program (sophomore or junior), but will consider all applicants
Physical Requirements:
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds and spend substantial time walking, standing, pulling, reaching, stooping, squatting, climbing ladders, bending, kneeling, and pushing/pulling objects such as drums and hazardous waste containers

Student Scholar Program: SDL provides unique opportunities for student employees to develop real-world experience and knowledge beyond the classroom through our Student Scholar Program. This program offers monthly technical workshops, outreach activities, and academic stipends to eligible student employees. All SDL student employees are invited to participate in the program to expand their professional network while supporting SDL's mission.
SDL delivers advanced multi-domain solutions to protect national security and enable scientific discovery. Our expertise in satellites, sensors and instruments, ground systems and data processing, and autonomous systems plays a critical role in missions supporting NASA and the Department of Defense. Join our team of engineers, scientists, technicians, and business professionals in our seventh decade of delivering mission success.

At SDL, we strive to uphold a culture of respect, collaboration, empowerment, and accountability. We listen with open minds, seek to understand diverse perspectives, and engage in thoughtful dialogue. We work together by sharing knowledge, involving others, and offering support. We trust and empower our team members to take ownership, act with integrity, and be accountable. Above all, we deliver on our commitments to each other and to our mission partners.

The application window for this position is expected to remain open for approximately 7 days; however, it may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. We encourage interested candidates to submit their applications promptly.

For questions, assistance, or accommodation with the application process or the DoD SkillBridge program, please contact employment@sdl.usu.edu.
